This intrinsic separation produces a substantial quality gap in resolution, color fidelity, and dynamic range between the cover photo and video frames. When users reselect an alternative frame from the video to replace an imperfect cover, the chosen frame often suffers from severe degradation, making direct replacement visually unsatisfactory. Restoring such frames requires simultaneous enhancement of spatial detail and color appearance, a task considerably more challenging than ordinary super-resolution or color enhancement. To address this, we define the Live Photo Cover Frame Reselection and Enhancement (LPRE) task, which leverages the intrinsic cues available within each Live Photo: the high-quality cover image as a structural and color reference, the user-reselected low-quality frame as the reconstruction target and several adjacent video frames providing temporal cues. Building upon this formulation, we construct Live2K, a real-world dataset of 2,042 Live Photos, and develop a unified one-stage baseline that integrates multi-frame fusion, guided color enhancement and super-resolution, establishing the first benchmark for Live Photo enhancement research.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the Live Photo Cover Frame Reselection and Enhancement (LPRE) task, addressing the quality gap between a Live Photo's computationally-processed cover image and its compressed video frames. The authors construct the Live2K dataset (2,042 Live Photos) and propose a unified one-stage baseline integrating multi-frame fusion, guided color enhancement, and super-resolution for restoring user-reselected low-quality frames.
AI.motivation: Modern smartphones capture Live Photos with a quality gap between the computationally-enhanced cover photo and the compressed video stream. When users reselect an alternative video frame to replace an imperfect cover, the chosen frame suffers from severe degradation (low resolution, poor color fidelity, limited dynamic range), making direct replacement visually unsatisfactory. Existing methods cannot simultaneously address spatial detail and color appearance enhancement for this specific task.
AI.method: The authors formulate the LPRE task, leveraging intrinsic cues within each Live Photo: the high-quality cover image (structural/color reference), the low-quality reselected frame (reconstruction target), and adjacent video frames (temporal cues). They construct the Live2K dataset of 2,042 real-world Live Photos and develop a unified one-stage baseline that integrates multi-frame fusion, guided color enhancement, and super-resolution.
AI.result: Construction of Live2K, a real-world dataset of 2,042 Live Photos. A unified one-stage baseline method is established, setting the first benchmark for Live Photo enhancement research.
AI.conclusion: The LPRE task addresses a practical smartphone photography problem. The proposed benchmark and baseline provide a foundation for future research in restoring user-reselected Live Photo frames to match the quality of computationally-processed cover images.

title: Uncertainty-aware damage identification in short-span bridges via physics-informed variational autoencoder
summary: Vibration-based damage identification in civil infrastructure is a challenging, ill-posed inverse problem due to measurement noise, sparse sensor arrays, and environmental variability. While deep learning is powerful for system identification, deterministic approaches lack reliable uncertainty quantification and can yield physically inconsistent results. This work proposes a robust probabilistic Scientific Machine Learning (SciML) framework: a physics-informed Gaussian copula variational autoencoder (PI-GCVAE) for structural health monitoring (SHM). First, we eliminate the need for data-driven surrogates by embedding a differentiable numerical eigenvalue solver directly into the VAE architecture. This ensures that latent space samples satisfy the governing equations of structural dynamics, reducing the trainable parameter space and improving generalization. Second, we replace the conventional independence assumption of latent variables with a Gaussian copula. This model captures complex, physics-dependent spatial cross-correlations between adjacent structural elements, defining feasible solutions while accounting for inherent system variability and measurement errors. Third, compared with alternatives such as Gaussian mixtures, our copula-based VAE provides an efficient distributional model for high-dimensional, strongly correlated latent spaces. We validate the approach using a synthetic dataset of a simply supported bridge subjected to various damage scenarios and corrupted with stochastic Gaussian noise. Synthetic data enables exhaustive validation against ground-truth stiffness values unavailable in practice. Results demonstrate that the PI-GCVAE accurately recovers the true posterior distribution, achieving 77.2% coverage. The proposed framework provides a reliable, scalable tool for early-stage damage diagnosis in operating bridges.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a physics-informed Gaussian copula variational autoencoder (PI-GCVAE) for vibration-based damage identification in civil infrastructure, embedding a differentiable eigenvalue solver into the VAE and using a Gaussian copula to model spatial correlations, achieving 77.2% coverage on synthetic bridge damage data.
AI.motivation: Vibration-based damage identification is an ill-posed inverse problem complicated by noise, sparse sensors, and environmental variability. Existing deep learning approaches lack reliable uncertainty quantification and can produce physically inconsistent results.
AI.method: The method embeds a differentiable numerical eigenvalue solver into the VAE architecture to enforce governing structural dynamics equations, and replaces the independence assumption of latent variables with a Gaussian copula to capture complex spatial cross-correlations between structural elements.
AI.result: Validated on a synthetic simply supported bridge dataset with stochastic Gaussian noise, the PI-GCVAE achieves 77.2% posterior coverage, accurately recovering the true posterior distribution of stiffness values.
AI.conclusion: The PI-GCVAE provides a reliable, scalable probabilistic SciML framework for early-stage damage diagnosis in operating bridges, offering efficient distributional modeling for high-dimensional correlated latent spaces compared to alternatives like Gaussian mixtures.

title: SeeMe: Mitigating Hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models through Effective Visual Token Engineering
summary: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in visual understanding tasks such as image captioning and visual question answering. However, they remain susceptible to hallucinations, generating content that is inconsistent with the actual visual input. Existing methods primarily intervene at the decoding stage, while overlooking a critical source of hallucinations: irrelevant or noisy visual tokens that mislead the decoding process. To address this issue, we propose SeeMe, a training-free framework that introduces the concept of feature engineering from traditional machine learning into LVLMs. SeeMe restructures visual tokens through a three-stage token engineering process to suppress hallucination sources while preserving informative visual evidence. Experiments on MME, POPE, and AMBER benchmarks across four LVLMs demonstrate that SeeMe consistently reduces hallucinations and improves output consistency, providing a novel perspective for mitigating hallucinations in LVLMs.

AI.tldr: SeeMe is a training-free framework that applies feature engineering to restructure visual tokens in LVLMs, reducing hallucinations by suppressing irrelevant/noisy visual tokens while preserving informative evidence.
AI.motivation: Existing hallucination mitigation methods primarily intervene at the decoding stage but overlook a critical source: irrelevant or noisy visual tokens that mislead the decoding process in LVLMs.
AI.method: SeeMe introduces feature engineering into LVLMs through a three-stage token engineering process that restructures visual tokens to suppress hallucination sources while keeping informative visual evidence. It is training-free.
AI.result: Experiments on MME, POPE, and AMBER benchmarks across four LVLMs show that SeeMe consistently reduces hallucinations and improves output consistency.
AI.conclusion: SeeMe provides a novel perspective for mitigating hallucinations in LVLMs by addressing noisy visual tokens at the feature level rather than only intervening at decoding.

title: CollabEval: Statistically Efficient Collaborative Model Evaluation via Matrix Completion
summary: Evaluating generative AI models is a routine, but resource-intensive, process that is conducted over and over again during the course of model development. In this work, we propose Collaborative Evaluation (CollabEval), a simple, effective, and principled method for exploiting dependencies between historical runs of different models on the same tasks to improve statistical efficiency. Specifically, our approach treats model evaluation as a matrix completion problem over an $M \times N$ matrix of evaluation scores, where $M$ is the total number of models and $N$ is the total number of evaluation prompts. We assume that a subset of these $M$ models are targeted for evaluation. For these target models only a small fraction, $p$, of prompts has been annotated with evaluation scores. Leveraging recent results in prediction-powered inference, we build a low-rank approximation of the score matrix, and use the reconstructed values as control variates in a manner that guarantees unbiased estimates of the true evaluation metric mean, in addition to statistically valid confidence intervals. Empirically, across a wide range of datasets, models, and sparsity levels $p$, we find that CollabEval substantially reduces the mean confidence interval size, and the mean squared error of the point estimate, compared to baseline methods at the same annotation budget.

AI.tldr: CollabEval leverages dependencies between historical model evaluations to improve statistical efficiency by treating model evaluation as a matrix completion problem, using low-rank approximation and prediction-powered inference for unbiased estimates with valid confidence intervals.
AI.motivation: Generative AI model evaluation is resource-intensive and conducted repeatedly during development. Current methods waste information from historical evaluation runs, motivating a more statistically efficient approach.
AI.method: Treats evaluation as an M×N matrix completion problem (M models, N prompts). For target models with only p% annotated scores, builds a low-rank approximation of the score matrix and uses reconstructed values as control variates via prediction-powered inference, guaranteeing unbiased estimates and valid confidence intervals.
AI.result: Across diverse datasets, models, and sparsity levels, CollabEval substantially reduces mean confidence interval size and mean squared error of point estimates compared to baselines at the same annotation budget.
AI.conclusion: Exploiting dependencies across historical model evaluations via matrix completion and prediction-powered inference provides a principled, efficient approach to generative AI evaluation with guaranteed statistical validity.

title: CritiqueDriveVLM: From Verifier-Guided Reinforcement Learning to Latent Thought Distillation for Autonomous Driving
summary: End-to-end Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show immense potential in autonomous driving. However, standard Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) often suffers from reasoning hallucinations and conservative biases. While traditional tool-augmented frameworks and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) approaches mitigate these issues, they incur exorbitant token consumption and unacceptable latency, rendering real-time deployment impractical. To resolve this reliability-efficiency trade-off, we propose CritiqueDriveVLM, a novel unified three-stage framework internalizing reasoning directly into the VLM. First, we introduce Critique-Driven Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning (RL) guided by a multi-dimensional verifier. By providing granular scalar feedback and a multi-turn penalty, we force the policy to internalize logical deduction, cultivating a robust System-2 Teacher that achieves high accuracy without fragile external tools. Subsequently, we propose Latent Thought Distillation to overcome the latency bottleneck. By aligning the Student's latent representations with the Teacher's fully converged reasoning states, we compress deep logical capabilities into a fast, CoT-free System-1 Student. Extensive experiments on the widely-used DriveLMM-01 benchmark demonstrate remarkable improvements. Compared to the base model, our tool-free Teacher significantly boosts Multiple Choice Quality (MCQ) from 55.54% to a state-of-the-art 76.54%. Crucially, our distilled Student preserves competitive reasoning depth while drastically minimizing generation length to an average of merely 28 tokens. This slashes inference latency by 88% (from 3482 ms to 416 ms), paving a highly robust pathway for low-latency autonomous driving.Our source code is available at https://github.com/MICLAB-BUPT/CritiqueDriveVLM.

AI.tldr: CritiqueDriveVLM is a three-stage framework that uses Critique-Driven Multi-Turn RL to internalize reasoning into VLMs (System-2 Teacher), then Latent Thought Distillation to compress reasoning into a fast, CoT-free System-1 Student, achieving 76.54% MCQ accuracy and 88% latency reduction (416 ms) on autonomous driving benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Standard SFT causes reasoning hallucinations and conservative biases in VLMs for autonomous driving. Existing tool-augmented and CoT methods improve reliability but incur excessive token consumption and latency, making real-time deployment impractical. The paper aims to resolve this reliability-efficiency trade-off.
AI.method: (1) Critique-Driven Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning (RL) with a multi-dimensional verifier providing granular scalar feedback and multi-turn penalty to internalize logical deduction into a System-2 Teacher. (2) Latent Thought Distillation that aligns Student's latent representations with Teacher's converged reasoning states, compressing deep logical capabilities into a fast, CoT-free System-1 Student.
AI.result: MCQ accuracy improved from 55.54% to 76.54% (Teacher). Distilled Student achieves competitive reasoning with only ~28 tokens average generation length, reducing inference latency by 88% (from 3482 ms to 416 ms).
AI.conclusion: The proposed CritiqueDriveVLM effectively resolves the reliability-efficiency trade-off in autonomous driving VLMs, enabling both high accuracy and low-latency real-time deployment without external tools or costly CoT reasoning.

title: KVpop -- Key-Value Cache Compression with Predictive Online Pruning
summary: Key-value (KV) cache growth is a major bottleneck in autoregressive decoding, as memory and bandwidth scale linearly with context length. Existing KV eviction methods often rely on static heuristics or proxy scores, which poorly track future token utility and cause brittle eviction as relevance shifts. To address this, we introduce KVpop, which learns a fixed-budget KV eviction policy by directly supervising the keep-or-drop decision. The scorer is trained against a novel future-attention target, computed efficiently without materializing dense attention maps. We further introduce a delayed memory-based scorer that, uniquely among learned eviction methods, defers scoring for a fixed number of steps to exploit near-future context. On AIME and HMMT mathematical reasoning, KVpop retains 98% of full-attention performance on Qwen3-4B at 75% KV cache compression and 97% at 88% compression, consistently outperforming established eviction baselines. Qwen3-8B shows even stronger results, reaching near-full teacher performance. These results show that supervising eviction with future-attention signals cuts memory costs while maintaining quality.

AI.tldr: KVpop learns a fixed-budget KV cache eviction policy supervised by a novel future-attention target, achieving 98% of full-attention performance at 75% compression on mathematical reasoning tasks.
AI.motivation: KV cache growth is a major bottleneck in autoregressive decoding, and existing eviction methods rely on static heuristics or proxy scores that poorly track future token utility and cause brittle eviction.
AI.method: Introduces KVpop with (1) a scorer trained against a future-attention target computed efficiently without dense attention maps, and (2) a delayed memory-based scorer that defers scoring for a fixed number of steps to exploit near-future context.
AI.result: On AIME and HMMT reasoning, KVpop retains 98% of full-attention performance at 75% KV cache compression and 97% at 88% compression on Qwen3-4B, with Qwen3-8B reaching near-full teacher performance, outperforming established eviction baselines.
AI.conclusion: Supervising eviction with future-attention signals cuts memory costs while maintaining quality, demonstrating that learned eviction policies with future-aware targets are effective.

title: Topology-Driven Transferability Estimation for 3D Medical Vision Foundation Models
summary: The growing number of medical vision foundation models highlights the need for effective model selection. However, mainstream selection methods rely on exhaustive fine-tuning, which is computationally expensive. Most of the existing Transferability Estimation (TE) metrics are primarily designed for image-level classification. They fail to preserve spatial relationships and fine-grained boundary details, which are crucial for the segmentation task. Additionally, while image-level tasks typically process a single feature vector per input, dense prediction tasks in 3D medical imaging require voxel-wise evaluation against dense annotations. To bridge these gaps, we propose a \textit{non-parametric, topology-driven} framework that estimates transferability directly from the alignment between the sparse 1-skeleton graph of dense features and semantic labels via Minimum Spanning Trees (MST). We decouple the alignment into two complementary geometric scales: Local Boundary-Aware Topological Consistency (LBTC) to assess boundary separability, where we prove that the MST leakage rate serves as a finite-sample lower bound on the Bayes error; and Global Representation Topology Divergence (GRTD) to evaluate the overall anatomical layout. Crucially, we formally justify a counterintuitive mechanism: Although without fine-tuning, the randomly initialized segmentation decoder acts as a topology-preserving spatial projector, reducing the variance of pairwise distance estimates and stabilizing global alignment evaluation. Fused via a task-adaptive gating mechanism, these dual metrics adapt to diverse clinical complexities. Evaluated on a large-scale benchmark of 114,000 3D medical volumes across diverse anatomical tasks, our topological framework achieves state-of-the-art transferability estimation with an average weighted Kendall (outperforming by 0.36) while accelerating evaluation by 56 times.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a non-parametric, topology-driven framework (using Minimum Spanning Trees and 1-skeleton graphs) for estimating transferability of medical vision foundation models for 3D segmentation, achieving state-of-the-art performance while being 56x faster than fine-tuning-based methods.
AI.motivation: Existing transferability estimation (TE) metrics are designed for image-level classification and fail to preserve spatial relationships and boundary details crucial for segmentation tasks. Also, fine-tuning-based model selection is computationally expensive. There is a need for efficient, segmentation-aware TE for 3D medical imaging.
AI.method: A topology-driven framework that (1) constructs sparse 1-skeleton graphs from dense features via Minimum Spanning Trees (MST), (2) decouples alignment into Local Boundary-Aware Topological Consistency (LBTC) assessing boundary separability via MST leakage rate (proven as a finite-sample lower bound on Bayes error), and (3) Global Representation Topology Divergence (GRTD) evaluating overall anatomical layout, fused via a task-adaptive gating mechanism. A randomly initialized segmentation decoder acts as a topology-preserving spatial projector.
AI.result: On a benchmark of 114,000 3D medical volumes across diverse anatomical tasks, the framework achieves state-of-the-art transferability estimation with an average weighted Kendall improvement of 0.36 and 56x acceleration over fine-tuning-based methods.
AI.conclusion: Topology-driven, non-parametric transferability estimation is both effective and efficient for 3D medical segmentation model selection, with theoretical guarantees linking MST leakage to Bayes error.

title: Computing Monetary Risk Measures in Linear Time
summary: Monetary risk measures have gained popularity for expressing decision-makers' risk aversion. Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Conditional-Value-at-Risk (CVaR), in particular, are used commonly for this purpose. This paper proposes new efficient algorithms to compute these risk measures for a discrete random variable in expected linear time with respect to the size of its domain. First, we propose a QuickVaR algorithm that computes the VaR of a discrete random variable. Then, we leverage QuickVaR to propose QuickDivergence, an algorithm for computing a class of $\varphi$-divergence risk measures, including the popular CVaR risk measure. The QuickVaR algorithm adapts the well-known Quickselect algorithm, while QuickDivergence builds on polymatroid optimization algorithms. Numerical results show that our new algorithms offer an order-of-magnitude speedup for large domains, and a library implementation of the algorithms is available at https://github.com/RiskAverseRL/RiskMeasures.jl.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes QuickVaR and QuickDivergence algorithms that compute Value-at-Risk and φ-divergence risk measures (including CVaR) for discrete random variables in expected linear time, leveraging Quickselect and polymatroid optimization, achieving order-of-magnitude speedups for large domains.
AI.motivation: Monetary risk measures like VaR and CVaR are widely used to express risk aversion, but computing them efficiently for discrete random variables with large domains remains computationally challenging.
AI.method: QuickVaR adapts the Quickselect algorithm for VaR computation; QuickDivergence builds on polymatroid optimization algorithms to compute φ-divergence risk measures including CVaR. Both achieve expected linear time complexity relative to domain size.
AI.result: The proposed algorithms offer an order-of-magnitude speedup for large domains compared to existing methods.
AI.conclusion: QuickVaR and QuickDivergence provide efficient, linear-time computation of VaR and CVaR for discrete random variables, with significant practical speedups and an open-source Julia library implementation.

title: Hierarchical Multi-to-Single-Modal Knowledge Distillation for Disruption Prediction in EAST
summary: Plasma disruption is a critical threat to tokamak safety. Existing data-driven predictors mainly rely on time-series diagnostic signals, while visible images provide complementary spatial cues including plasma deformation, local brightening, and radiation-structure evolution. Although the image modality improves the model's discriminative capability, it also substantially increases the computational cost during inference. To address this issue, we propose a hierarchical multi-to-single-modal knowledge distillation framework for disruption prediction on a synchronized EAST multimodal dataset. During training, visible images and time-series signals are used to train a multimodal teacher, which learns disruption precursor representations through Transformer-based encoders and a prototype-guided spatiotemporal hypergraph module. During inference, only the time-series student is retained, with multimodal knowledge transferred through graph-structure-level, representation-level, and decision-level distillation. On the 640-discharge EAST dataset, the results demonstrate that the proposed framework can preserve the discriminative advantages of multimodal learning while substantially reducing inference cost, and providing an effective route for efficient disruption prediction in EAST. The source code of this paper will be released on https://github.com/Event-AHU/OpenFusion.

AI.tldr: A hierarchical multi-to-single-modal knowledge distillation framework is proposed for plasma disruption prediction in tokamaks, using a multimodal teacher (visible images + time-series signals) during training but only a time-series student during inference, achieving efficient prediction with preserved discriminative performance on EAST data.
AI.motivation: Plasma disruption poses critical threats to tokamak safety. While visible images improve prediction accuracy by providing spatial cues, they substantially increase inference computational cost. The goal is to retain multimodal learning advantages while reducing inference overhead.
AI.method: A hierarchical multi-to-single-modal knowledge distillation framework: (1) A multimodal teacher with Transformer-based encoders and a prototype-guided spatiotemporal hypergraph module learns from both visible images and time-series signals. (2) Knowledge is transferred to a time-series-only student via graph-structure-level, representation-level, and decision-level distillation. (3) Only the student is used during inference.
AI.result: On a 640-discharge EAST multimodal dataset, the framework preserves the discriminative advantages of multimodal learning while substantially reducing inference cost.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework provides an effective route for efficient disruption prediction in EAST, balancing performance and computational efficiency.

title: FAST: A Holistic Framework for Optimizing Memory-I/O, Computation, and Sampling in Temporal GNN Training
summary: Temporal Graph Neural Networks (TGNNs) are widely used for learning from dynamic graphs in applications such as recommendation, social network analysis, and traffic forecasting. However, scaling TGNN training to large dynamic graphs remains challenging due to three intertwined bottlenecks: memory I/O, irregular computation, and temporal neighbor sampling. Existing systems often optimize these stages in isolation, leaving substantial performance headroom on the table. We present FAST, a holistic framework that accelerates end-to-end TGNN training by jointly optimizing sampling, memory I/O, and computation. FAST introduces SlimCache, which exploits within-batch compression and cross-batch caching to reduce host-device data movement under limited GPU memory budgets. It further designs thread-efficient graph operators tailored to sparse temporal subgraphs, improving GPU cache locality and reducing the latency of aggregation and edge softmax. In addition, FAST employs a topology-aware sampling strategy that improves CPU cache locality and accelerates temporal neighbor sampling. Extensive experiments on real-world large dynamic graphs show that FAST achieves an average of 2.1x (up to 4.7x) speedup over state-of-the-art systems without sacrificing model accuracy.

AI.tldr: FAST is a holistic framework for accelerating TGNN training on large dynamic graphs, achieving 2.1x-4.7x speedup over state-of-the-art systems through joint optimization of sampling, memory I/O, and computation.
AI.motivation: Scaling TGNN training to large dynamic graphs is challenging due to three intertwined bottlenecks: memory I/O, irregular computation, and temporal neighbor sampling. Existing systems optimize these stages in isolation, leaving substantial performance headroom.
AI.method: FAST introduces three key components: (1) SlimCache for within-batch compression and cross-batch caching to reduce host-device data movement; (2) thread-efficient graph operators tailored to sparse temporal subgraphs for improved GPU cache locality; (3) topology-aware sampling strategy that improves CPU cache locality and accelerates temporal neighbor sampling.
AI.result: On real-world large dynamic graphs, FAST achieves an average of 2.1x (up to 4.7x) speedup over state-of-the-art systems without sacrificing model accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Jointly optimizing sampling, memory I/O, and computation in a holistic manner significantly outperforms isolated optimization approaches for TGNN training on large dynamic graphs.

title: HeartVolMesh: Cardiac Volumetric Mesh Reconstruction via Covariance-Guided Graph Deformation
summary: Accurate patient-specific tetrahedral cardiac meshes are essential for in-silico trials, yet common segmentation-then-modelling pipelines can blur thin-wall anatomy and offer limited cross-case correspondence. We propose HeartVolMesh, which lifts each template vertex to an anisotropic Gaussian kernel and uses a 3D CNN-GNN to predict per-vertex displacements and Cholesky-parameterized covariances from volumetric images. Training is guided by a covariance-aware negative log-likelihood loss with lightweight mesh regularization. For volumetric meshing, we warp a fixed tetrahedral template to the reconstructed surface via staged alignment, non-rigid registration, and deformation propagation, preserving connectivity and correspondence by construction, with resolution controlled by template density. Experiments show consistent gains over deformation-based baselines in surface mesh accuracy and volumetric mesh fidelity.

AI.tldr: HeartVolMesh uses anisotropic Gaussian kernels and a 3D CNN-GNN to predict per-vertex displacements from volumetric images, enabling accurate tetrahedral cardiac meshes with preserved cross-case correspondence via template warping.
AI.motivation: Accurate patient-specific tetrahedral cardiac meshes are essential for in-silico trials, but existing segmentation-then-modelling pipelines blur thin-wall anatomy and offer limited cross-case correspondence.
AI.method: Lifts each template vertex to an anisotropic Gaussian kernel, uses a 3D CNN-GNN to predict per-vertex displacements and Cholesky-parameterized covariances, trains with covariance-aware NLL loss and mesh regularization, and warps a fixed tetrahedral template via staged alignment, non-rigid registration, and deformation propagation.
AI.result: Consistent gains over deformation-based baselines in both surface mesh accuracy and volumetric mesh fidelity.
AI.conclusion: HeartVolMesh achieves accurate volumetric cardiac meshes with preserved correspondence and controllable resolution, outperforming deformation-based approaches.

title: Functional Bilevel Optimization for Predictive Fairness
summary: When sensitive attributes are continuous and high-dimensional $-$ demographic score vectors, posteriors over attributes, age or income profiles $-$ enforcing full statistical independence is often too restrictive, and existing relaxations rely on indirect dependence penalties or adversarial schemes that do not directly target the fairness-accuracy trade-off. We instead consider mean demographic parity through DPVar, the variance of the conditional-mean prediction given the sensitive attribute, and show that optimizing it yields a functional bilevel problem. We propose two algorithms for this problem: FBO, which uses a closed-form adjoint we derive for the squared-loss case to obtain an exact hypergradient, and ITD, which differentiates through unrolled inner steps and extends beyond squared loss. On synthetic data and a new semi-synthetic benchmark built from 60 tabular regression datasets, both methods achieve the lowest or near-lowest aggregate fairness-accuracy regret, and consistently match or outperform strong HSIC, adversarial, linear-dependence, and generalized-DP baselines.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes mean demographic parity via DPVar (variance of conditional-mean predictions given sensitive attributes) for handling continuous, high-dimensional sensitive attributes, formulating it as a bilevel optimization problem. Two algorithms are introduced: FBO (exact hypergradient via adjoint for squared loss) and ITD (unrolled differentiation for general losses). Both achieve near-optimal fairness-accuracy trade-offs on synthetic data and 60 tabular regression datasets, outperforming HSIC, adversarial, and other baselines.
AI.motivation: Existing fairness relaxations for continuous/high-dimensional sensitive attributes rely on indirect penalties or adversarial methods that do not directly optimize the fairness-accuracy trade-off, and full statistical independence is too restrictive.
AI.method: Formulates mean demographic parity (DPVar) as a functional bilevel optimization problem; proposes FBO (adjoint-based exact hypergradient for squared loss) and ITD (implicit differentiation through unrolled steps for general losses).
AI.result: Both methods achieve the lowest or near-lowest aggregate fairness-accuracy regret on synthetic data and 60 tabular regression datasets, consistently matching or outperforming HSIC, adversarial, linear-dependence, and generalized-DP baselines.
AI.conclusion: Directly targeting DPVar via bilevel optimization yields superior fairness-accuracy trade-offs compared to existing indirect or adversarial approaches for continuous sensitive attributes.

title: Beyond Random Sampling: Distribution-Aware Alignment for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
summary: Precise medical image segmentation is crucial for clinical diagnosis and treatment planning, yet relies heavily on expensive expert annotations. Semi-supervised medical image segmentation (SSMIS) offers a cost-effective solution but typically operates under the assumption of independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) data, defaulting to random sampling. While statistically valid at scale, this strategy suffers from severe representation bias in low-data regimes, failing to capture the heterogeneous medical data manifold. To address this, we propose a highly data-efficient framework driven by distribution alignment. First, we introduce an offline Distribution-Aware Sample Selection strategy. By leveraging Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) and our designed Density-K-Center algorithm, we explicitly identify representative structural anchors, establishing a more representative labeled domain. Second, to bridge the remaining distribution gap, we propose the Memory-guided Copy-Paste (MCP) module. Tailored for the inherent class imbalance in medical scans, MCP leverages a semantic memory mechanism to retrieve historically consistent priors for cross-domain alignment, encouraging semantic consistency. Coupled with an easy-to-hard progressive schedule, this framework effectively mitigates early-stage pseudo-label noise. Extensive experiments on six diverse 2D and 3D datasets demonstrate strong segmentation performance, particularly in extremely low-labeled scenarios (\eg, 1/16 ratio).

AI.tldr: Proposes a distribution-aligned semi-supervised framework for medical image segmentation that uses VFMs and Density-K-Center for representative sample selection and Memory-guided Copy-Paste with progressive learning to bridge distribution gap, achieving strong performance even at 1/16 labeling ratio.
AI.motivation: Standard SSMIS assumes i.i.d. data and uses random sampling, which causes severe representation bias in low-data regimes and fails to capture heterogeneous medical data manifolds.
AI.method: (1) Offline Distribution-Aware Sample Selection using VFMs and Density-K-Center algorithm to identify representative structural anchors. (2) Memory-guided Copy-Paste (MCP) module with semantic memory mechanism for cross-domain alignment and class imbalance handling, plus an easy-to-hard progressive schedule to reduce early pseudo-label noise.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on six 2D/3D datasets demonstrate strong segmentation performance, especially in extremely low-labeled scenarios (e.g., 1/16 ratio).
AI.conclusion: Distribution alignment via representative sample selection and memory-guided semantic consistency is highly effective for data-efficient semi-supervised medical image segmentation under extreme label scarcity.

title: Counterfactual Methods for Detecting Unfairness in Anti-Money Laundering Algorithms
summary: The application of machine learning-based predictive algorithms to Anti-Money Laundering (AML) has grown rapidly, driven by the vast volume of financial transaction data available to banks. These algorithms are typically trained not only on transactional data but also on sensitive client information, which may raise fairness concerns. Despite this, AML detection systems remain largely underexplored from a fairness perspective, even though deeper analytical methods based on counterfactuals are now available. Such techniques enable the decomposition of the direct and indirect effects of potentially sensitive features on model predictions, thereby supporting the evaluation of whether their influence is acceptable from a fairness perspective. Closing this gap, we consider the synthetic IBM AMLSim transaction dataset and construct additional features of the country of an account and its average behaviour. This improves the predictive performance of diverse machine learning models, ranging from baseline decision trees to state-of-the-art graph neural networks. We assess the potential unfairness associated with these features through a counterfactual, path-specific effect analysis. This reveals that fairness violations tend to be more pronounced for models whose predictive performance benefits the most from the extended features. Such a finding highlights a concrete instance of the trade-off between predictive accuracy and fairness in AML applications, thus underscoring the urgency of a systematic fairness analysis in such critical domains.

AI.tldr: This paper examines fairness in AML machine learning models by adding country and average behavior features to the IBM AMLSim dataset. Using counterfactual path-specific effect analysis, it finds that models with better predictive performance from these features exhibit greater fairness violations, revealing a trade-off between accuracy and fairness in AML.
AI.motivation: AML detection systems remain underexplored from a fairness perspective despite using sensitive client data; the paper aims to close this gap by systematically evaluating fairness in AML models using counterfactual analysis methods.
AI.method: The authors use the synthetic IBM AMLSim transaction dataset, construct country and average behavior features, train multiple ML models (from decision trees to graph neural networks), and assess unfairness via counterfactual, path-specific effect analysis to decompose direct and indirect effects of sensitive features.
AI.result: Fairness violations are more pronounced for models whose predictive performance benefits most from the extended features, demonstrating a concrete trade-off between predictive accuracy and fairness in AML applications.
AI.conclusion: The findings underscore the urgency of systematic fairness analysis in AML domains, as improving model accuracy via sensitive features can exacerbate unfairness.

title: AdaptiveSplat:Texture Aware Controllable 3D Gaussian Allocation for Feed-Forward Reconstruction
summary: Current feed-forward 3D reconstruction methods predict pixel aligned Gaussian primitives, resulting in highly redundant representations. A natural solution is to prune the redundant Gaussians, but naive pruning introduces severe artifacts and often requires inference time fine-tuning, breaking the feed-forward paradigm. Based on previous works, high frequency regions require more Gaussian primitives, while low frequency regions can be represented with significantly fewer primitives. Motivated by this, we propose a novel approach to explicitly control the number of Gaussians by leveraging local texture information. Our approach achieves this through three key components: (1) texture estimation to capture spatial variation in scene detail, (2) texture-aware pruning that removes redundant Gaussians from low frequency regions, and (3) an adaptive Gaussian head that predicts the modified attributes of the retained primitives without breaking the feed-forward paradigm. Experiments on RE10K, ACID, DL3DV, Tanks and Temples, and DTU demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, while ablation studies validate the contributions of its key components.

AI.tldr: A feed-forward 3D reconstruction method that explicitly controls the number of Gaussian primitives by pruning redundant Gaussians from low-frequency regions based on local texture information, without requiring inference-time fine-tuning.
AI.motivation: Current feed-forward 3D reconstruction methods produce highly redundant pixel-aligned Gaussian representations. Naive pruning introduces artifacts and often requires inference-time fine-tuning, breaking the feed-forward paradigm. The authors aim to reduce redundancy without sacrificing quality or violating the feed-forward setup.
AI.method: Three components: (1) texture estimation to capture spatial variation in scene detail, (2) texture-aware pruning that removes redundant Gaussians from low-frequency regions, and (3) an adaptive Gaussian head that predicts modified attributes for retained primitives, all within a feed-forward paradigm.
AI.result: Evaluated on RE10K, ACID, DL3DV, Tanks and Temples, and DTU datasets. Ablation studies validate contributions of each key component.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach effectively controls Gaussian redundancy via texture-aware pruning while maintaining the feed-forward paradigm and reconstruction quality.

title: Choosing a parallel heterogeneous ensemble method for tabular classification
summary:
Parallel ensemble methods were compared on $56$ small-to-medium tabular classification tasks drawn from OpenML CC18. A set of ``best practice'' recommendations on the use of ensemble methods was derived from these observations. It was later validated on 28 additional tasks using TabArena's precomputed data, where the recommendation set significantly outperformed Single Best and matched or exceeded individual ensemble methods.
  Two key observations were made. First, Blending and Stacking are inconsistent, but their inconsistencies are independent and happen on different tasks. Second, while Hard Voting's probabilistic classification is rather weak, a consequence of using vote proportions as posterior estimates, Robust Soft Voting's probabilistic classification is particularly successful, especially in the multiclass case.

AI.tldr: Parallel ensemble methods were compared on 56 classification tasks, deriving best-practice recommendations that significantly outperformed Single Best and matched individual ensemble methods when validated on 28 additional tasks. Key findings: Blending and Stacking have independent inconsistencies; Robust Soft Voting excels in probabilistic classification, especially for multiclass problems.
AI.motivation: To derive and validate best-practice recommendations for using parallel ensemble methods on small-to-medium tabular classification tasks, addressing inconsistencies in Blending and Stacking and the probabilistic weakness of Hard Voting.
AI.method: Compared parallel ensemble methods on 56 OpenML CC18 tabular classification tasks, derived best-practice recommendations, then validated on 28 additional tasks using TabArena's precomputed data.
AI.result: The recommendation set significantly outperformed Single Best and matched/exceeded individual ensemble methods. Blending and Stacking inconsistencies are independent. Robust Soft Voting's probabilistic classification is particularly successful, especially for multiclass cases.
AI.conclusion: A validated set of best-practice recommendations for parallel ensemble methods was produced, with Robust Soft Voting being notably effective for probabilistic classification.

title: EMPURPLE: A Free Lunch for Diffusion Distillation based on the Information Bottleneck
summary: Diffusion models achieve impressive image-generation quality but remain expensive at inference time. Diffusion distillation reduces sampling steps, yet many distilled models, including SDXL-Lightning and distribution matching distillation methods, suffer from degraded Fréchet Inception Distance (FID). We analyze this phenomenon through a PAC-style generalization bound. Our analysis suggests that aggressive early-step redirection of the velocity field makes the distillation target harder to learn, enlarging the train-test gap. As a result, early-step output distributions differ between training and inference, causing distribution mismatch in the intermediate noisy latent used as next-step inputs. We empirically validate this mechanism by showing reduced diversity in both intermediate features and final outputs. To address this issue, we propose EMPURPLE, a simple training-free method that recycles intermediate latents sampled from the original model. EMPURPLE is model-agnostic and improves FID by 7\% to 20\% across DMD2, Hyper-SD, FlashSD, and SDXL-Lightning. The repo is: https://github.com/TheLovesOfLadyPurple/Empurple-Training-Free-Algorithm-To-enhance-Diversity-of-The-Diffusion-Distillation-Model

AI.tldr: Diffusion distillation models suffer from degraded FID due to distribution mismatch from aggressive early-step velocity field redirection. EMPURPLE, a training-free method that recycles intermediate latents from the original model, improves FID by 7-20% across multiple distilled models.
AI.motivation: Distilled diffusion models (e.g., SDXL-Lightning, DMD) reduce sampling steps but suffer from degraded FID. The authors aim to analyze and address this performance degradation.
AI.method: The authors propose EMPURPLE, a training-free method that recycles intermediate latents sampled from the original (non-distilled) diffusion model to mitigate distribution mismatch during inference.
AI.result: EMPURPLE improves FID by 7% to 20% across DMD2, Hyper-SD, FlashSD, and SDXL-Lightning.
AI.conclusion: Aggressive early-step velocity field redirection enlarges the train-test gap in distilled diffusion models, causing distribution mismatch. EMPURPLE effectively mitigates this issue and is model-agnostic.

title: Grokking Is Conditional and Fragile: A Fully-Tractable, Multi-Seed Study at 12K Parameters
summary: Grokking -- the delayed onset of generalization long after a network has fit its training set - -is usually studied in models too large to read completely and reported from single training runs. We instead study a publicly released ~11,856-parameter Llama-style transformer (Glimmer-1-Base) on modular arithmetic, small enough to enumerate its weights, attention, and full input-output map, and we measure grokking as a multi-seed rate rather than a single outcome. In this fully-tractable regime grokking is a conditional, fragile phase transition. It is gated by training-set coverage, whose threshold tracks output cardinality (the modulus) more than task structure, an ordering that holds above the transition and across a ten-fold change in domain size. Weight decay reproduces the Omnigrok inverted-U at 12K parameters, a positive control on the rate measurement. Grokking also sits on a numerical knife-edge: two perturbations of the floating-point environment -- CPU thread count (reduction order) and CPU-versus-GPU execution -- each flip a minority of same-seed outcomes without a detectable shift in the aggregate rate. Decomposition into sub-task specialists helps chiefly by making coverage cheap rather than by adding supervision. Methodologically, multi-seed control under a fixed numerical environment overturns three dramatic single-run narratives in our own data, each a seed confound. The unit of evidence for grokking must therefore be a multi-seed rate under a pinned numerical environment, checked where possible against a direct reading of the model.

AI.tldr: This paper studies grokking in a fully-tractable 11,856-parameter Llama-style transformer (Glimmer-1-Base) on modular arithmetic. Using multi-seed rate measurements rather than single runs, the authors find grokking is a conditional, fragile phase transition gated by training-set coverage, sensitive to numerical precision (CPU thread count, CPU vs. GPU), and that weight decay reproduces the Omnigrok inverted-U. They show that single-run narratives can be confounded by seed choice, arguing grokking evidence requires multi-seed rates under pinned numerical environments.
AI.motivation: Grokking is typically studied in large models with single training runs, making it difficult to systematically analyze the phenomenon. The authors aim to study grokking in a fully tractable small transformer where the entire weight space, attention patterns, and input-output map can be enumerated, enabling rigorous multi-seed statistical analysis.
AI.method: The authors train an 11,856-parameter Llama-style transformer (Glimmer-1-Base) on modular arithmetic tasks. They measure grokking as a multi-seed rate (across many random seeds) rather than a single-run outcome. They systematically vary training-set coverage, weight decay, numerical environment (CPU thread count, CPU vs. GPU execution), and analyze sub-task specialist decomposition.
AI.result: (1) Grokking is a conditional, fragile phase transition gated by training-set coverage, with threshold tracking output cardinality (modulus). (2) Weight decay reproduces the Omnigrok inverted-U at 12K parameters. (3) Grokking is numerically sensitive: CPU thread count and CPU-vs-GPU execution flip minority of same-seed outcomes without shifting aggregate rate. (4) Decomposition into sub-task specialists helps mainly by making coverage cheap. (5) Multi-seed control overturns three dramatic single-run narratives that were seed confounds.
AI.conclusion: The unit of evidence for grokking must be a multi-seed rate under a pinned numerical environment, checked where possible against a direct reading of the model. Single-run narratives are unreliable due to seed and numerical environment confounds.

title: AquaStereo: Enabling Underwater Stereo Matching via Depth-Conditioned Diffusion and Geometry Self-Distillation
summary: Learning-based stereo matching models struggle in underwater environments due to scarce in-domain data and the difficulty of extracting discriminative correspondences from degraded imagery. In this work, we present $\textbf{AquaStereo}$, a perception-enhanced framework with a data simulation pipeline and a self-distillation strategy that jointly address data scarcity and feature degradation in underwater stereo matching. First, a depth-conditioned diffusion pipeline renders underwater stereo pairs while preserving binocular geometry, with a lightweight left-right consistency module ensuring geometric alignment. Training on this synthetic corpus effectively narrows the terrestrial-underwater gap and improves zero-shot robustness. Second, a frozen binocular teacher trained on clean terrestrial pairs guides a student exposed to rendered underwater pairs with perturbations. A stage-weighted sequence loss is performed to align the student's disparities with the teacher's geometry, while a clean-branch supervision with shared pseudo targets prevents scale drift. To further enhance feature stability under turbidity and low texture, we introduce learnable perception frames, a perception-enhanced feature formulation that constructs robust matching descriptors by fusing temporal cues from two auxiliary views encoded by a video backbone with semantic features extracted by a strong image encoder. Extensive experiments demonstrate that $\textbf{AquaStereo}$ substantially improves robustness and zero-shot generalization in challenging underwater scenarios. The code is available at https://github.com/qz-wei/AquaStereo.

AI.tldr: AquaStereo is a learning-based stereo matching framework for underwater environments that addresses data scarcity and feature degradation using a depth-conditioned diffusion data simulation pipeline and a self-distillation strategy with perception-enhanced features (learnable perception frames) to improve robustness and zero-shot generalization.
AI.motivation: Learning-based stereo matching models struggle in underwater environments due to scarce in-domain data and difficulty extracting discriminative correspondences from degraded imagery (turbidity, low texture). The paper aims to jointly address data scarcity and feature degradation.
AI.method: (1) A depth-conditioned diffusion pipeline that renders underwater stereo pairs with a left-right consistency module for geometric alignment. (2) A self-distillation strategy where a frozen binocular teacher (trained on clean terrestrial pairs) guides a student exposed to rendered underwater pairs with perturbations, using stage-weighted sequence loss and clean-branch supervision to prevent scale drift. (3) Learnable perception frames that fuse temporal cues from auxiliary views (via a video backbone) with semantic features (via a strong image encoder) for robust matching descriptors.
AI.result: AquaStereo substantially improves robustness and zero-shot generalization in challenging underwater scenarios compared to existing methods.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework effectively bridges the terrestrial-underwater domain gap and enhances feature stability under turbidity and low texture, enabling reliable stereo matching in underwater settings.

title: Localized LoRA-MoE: Block-wise Low-Rank Experts With Adaptive Routing
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) and high-dimensional perception networks increasingly rely on parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) to adapt to diverse operational contexts. However, standard methods like LoRA are structurally limited by a monolithic bottleneck, making them highly susceptible to gradient warfare. Interleaved multi-task streams may trigger destructive optimization feedback, collapsing adapter weights into unspecialized averages. While recent spatial partitioning methods have introduced block-wise isolation, they remain trapped in static topologies, unable to adapt to dynamic task-switching or environmental sensor failure. In this work, we introduce Localized LoRA-MoE, a unified framework that fuses localized spatial blocking with dynamic, context-conditioned routing. We propose and evaluate two novel architectural paradigms: Block-Wise LoRA-MoE (Centralized Macro-Routing), which modulates the entire structural grid via a monolithic context signal, and Cell-Wise LoRA-MoE (Decentralized Micro-Routing), which empowers every coordinate cell in the matrix grid with autonomous, localized expert gating. Through a comprehensive suite of benchmarks, ranging from high-dimensional SVD matrix simulations and real-world tabular transformations to spatial vision perception under sensor degradation, we demonstrate that both architectures resolve optimization deadlocks inherent in static baselines. Our empirical results establish that decentralized cell-level gating achieves complete statistical parity with an omniscient global coordinator, providing a robust "gradient firewall" that protects surviving pathways from fault-propagated corruption. Our proposals consistently outperform static baselines, offering a scalable and parameter-efficient solution for dynamic model adaptation across granular coordinate fields and shifting operational regimes.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Localized LoRA-MoE, a unified framework combining localized spatial blocking with dynamic context-conditioned routing for parameter-efficient fine-tuning. Two architectures are proposed: Block-Wise LoRA-MoE (centralized macro-routing) and Cell-Wise LoRA-MoE (decentralized micro-routing). The decentralized approach achieves complete statistical parity with an omniscient global coordinator while providing a "gradient firewall" against fault propagation, outperforming static baselines across benchmarks including SVD simulations, tabular transformations, and spatial vision under sensor degradation.
AI.motivation: Standard PEFT methods like LoRA suffer from structural limitations due to monolithic bottlenecks, causing gradient warfare and unspecialized weight collapse in multi-task settings. Existing spatial partitioning methods remain trapped in static topologies unable to handle dynamic task-switching or sensor failure.
AI.method: Localized LoRA-MoE framework with two paradigms: (1) Block-Wise LoRA-MoE (Centralized Macro-Routing) using monolithic context signals to modulate the entire structural grid, and (2) Cell-Wise LoRA-MoE (Decentralized Micro-Routing) enabling each coordinate cell with autonomous, localized expert gating.
AI.result: Both architectures resolve optimization deadlocks inherent in static baselines. Decentralized cell-level gating achieves complete statistical parity with an omniscient global coordinator and provides a robust "gradient firewall" protecting surviving pathways from fault-propagated corruption. The proposals consistently outperform static baselines across all benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Localized LoRA-MoE offers a scalable, parameter-efficient solution for dynamic model adaptation across granular coordinate fields and shifting operational regimes, with decentralized micro-routing being particularly robust against gradient warfare and fault propagation.

title: Road-Aware Anomaly Segmentation with Query-Guided Polygons and CLIP in Autonomous Driving
comment: Accepted to IEEE IV26. Code is available at https://github.com/chrisyan/RAAS
summary: Traditional semantic segmentation models operate under a closed-set assumption and struggle to recognize unknown or unexpected objects-an essential capability for autonomous driving. As a result, such models often misclassify or overlook out-of-distribution (OOD) road anomalies, posing safety risks in open-world environments. We present a lightweight, postprocessing, road-aware anomaly segmentation framework that requires no retraining, no OOD data, and no auxiliary supervision. Our approach builds on a mask transformer-based segmentation network by exploiting query-level mask confidence and deriving a polygonal road prior to detect gap regions that may correspond to anomalies. To further suppress false positives, we introduce a CLIP-based zero-shot semantic filtering module using in-distribution prompts, with optional generalized OOD prompts. By jointly leveraging spatial priors and semantic verification, our framework produces robust and interpretable anomaly predictions. Evaluation on three public benchmarks-Fishyscapes, SMIYC, and RoadAnomaly-shows consistently strong performance. In particular, our method outperforms the training-free baseline Maskomaly on most metrics and achieves the highest AP on Fishyscapes LostAndFound. These results demonstrate the practicality and deployability of our approach for real-world autonomous driving systems.

AI.tldr: A lightweight, training-free anomaly segmentation framework for autonomous driving that combines mask transformer query confidence, polygonal road priors, and CLIP-based zero-shot filtering to detect road anomalies without retraining or OOD data.
AI.motivation: Traditional closed-set segmentation models fail to recognize unknown road anomalies in open-world autonomous driving, leading to safety risks due to misclassification or oversight of OOD objects.
AI.method: Builds on a mask transformer segmentation network by exploiting query-level mask confidence and deriving a polygonal road prior to detect gap regions. A CLIP-based zero-shot semantic filtering module with in-distribution and optional OOD prompts suppresses false positives, combining spatial priors with semantic verification.
AI.result: Outperforms the training-free baseline Maskomaly on most metrics across Fishyscapes, SMIYC, and RoadAnomaly benchmarks, achieving the highest AP on Fishyscapes LostAndFound.
AI.conclusion: The approach demonstrates practicality and deployability for real-world autonomous driving systems, offering robust and interpretable anomaly predictions without retraining or auxiliary supervision.

title: PDEFlow: Autonomous Agentic PDE Pipelines for Neural Operator Learning and Solver-Free Inference
summary: We present PDEFlow, an autonomous agentic framework that turns user-level ODE and PDE descriptions into solver-backed neural-operator pipelines. The workflow links problem specification, data generation, operator training, and checkpoint-based inference. A stateful input graph converts multi-turn natural-language input and user edits into validated problem specifications. The data-generation module then samples parameters, solves the configured governing-equation with FEniCSx finite-element backend, and stores the solutions as operator-ready tensors. The training and inference stages use a registry-based interface, allowing different neural operators to be trained and deployed without changing the surrounding pipeline. In the current implementation, we instantiate this interface with a multi-branch Bayesian DeepONet. Experiments on benchmark ODE and PDE tasks show that PDEFlow can construct valid specifications, generate solver-backed datasets, train neural operators across steady and transient problem classes, and provide solver-free predictions from saved checkpoints. The framework is designed for repeatable scientific and engineering workflows where many related physics configurations must be specified, simulated, learned, and queried with minimal manual intervention.

AI.tldr: PDEFlow is an autonomous agentic framework that converts user-level ODE/PDE descriptions into solver-backed neural-operator pipelines, enabling specification, data generation, training, and inference with minimal manual intervention.
AI.motivation: To automate and streamline the end-to-end workflow of specifying, simulating, learning, and querying physics problems across many related configurations, reducing manual intervention in scientific and engineering workflows.
AI.method: A stateful input graph handles multi-turn natural-language input and user edits for problem specification; data generation uses FEniCSx finite-element backend to sample parameters and solve governing equations; a registry-based interface enables different neural operators (instantiated with a multi-branch Bayesian DeepONet) to be trained and deployed without pipeline changes.
AI.result: PDEFlow constructs valid specifications, generates solver-backed datasets, trains neural operators across steady and transient problem classes, and provides solver-free predictions from saved checkpoints on benchmark ODE and PDE tasks.
AI.conclusion: The framework is designed for repeatable scientific and engineering workflows where many related physics configurations must be specified, simulated, learned, and queried with minimal manual intervention, and the current implementation demonstrates feasibility on benchmark tasks.

title: Aura: Consistent Multi-Subject Video Generation via VLM-Grounded Semantic Alignment
summary: Subject-driven and multi-element video generation are central to controllable video synthesis, but existing methods still struggle to preserve identity consistency and model complex relationships among multiple subjects. In this paper, we propose Aura, a unified framework for high-fidelity and identity-consistent video generation. To better capture scene dynamics and subject interactions, we introduce AI director-level captions that provide dense and structured descriptions of video content. We further leverage a vision-language model (VLM) with learnable queries to extract multimodal semantic features from textual and visual references, covering both global semantics and fine-grained visual cues. To bridge the representational gap between the VLM and the Diffusion Transformer (DiT), we design a two-stage alignment strategy that progressively maps VLM features into the DiT feature space. For visual conditioning, we adopt token concatenation to inject reference information directly into the generation process. To distinguish heterogeneous subject types and reduce common copy-paste artifacts, we develop a subject-aware RoPE-Shift mechanism. To further differentiate reference images of different categories, we introduce subject-aware learnable tokens. In addition, we introduce Memory Tokens to balance the training signal across examples with different numbers of reference subjects. During inference, Progressive-APG (Adaptive Prompt Guidance) further alleviates oversaturation and improves semantic alignment with user prompts. Finally, we build a high-quality video-subject image dataset through a dedicated data construction pipeline. Extensive experiments show that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on both single-subject generation and more challenging multi-element scenarios.

AI.tldr: Aura is a unified framework for high-fidelity, identity-consistent video generation that handles both single- and multi-subject scenarios by combining AI director-level captions, a VLM with learnable queries, a two-stage alignment strategy to bridge VLM and DiT representations, token concatenation for visual conditioning, subject-aware RoPE-Shift and learnable tokens to distinguish heterogeneous subjects, Memory Tokens for balancing training signals, and Progressive-APG for improved inference. It achieves SOTA results on single and multi-element video generation tasks.
AI.motivation: Existing methods for subject-driven and multi-element video generation fail to preserve identity consistency and model complex relationships among multiple subjects.
AI.method: (1) AI director-level captions for dense structured video descriptions; (2) VLM with learnable queries to extract multimodal semantic features; (3) two-stage alignment strategy to map VLM features into DiT space; (4) token concatenation for visual conditioning; (5) subject-aware RoPE-Shift and learnable tokens to handle heterogeneous subjects and reduce copy-paste artifacts; (6) Memory Tokens to balance training across varying numbers of reference subjects; (7) Progressive-APG for inference to reduce oversaturation and improve semantic alignment.
AI.result: State-of-the-art performance on both single-subject generation and more challenging multi-element scenarios, validated through extensive experiments.
AI.conclusion: Aura provides a robust unified framework that significantly improves identity consistency and complex subject interaction modeling in controllable video synthesis.

title: Physiological Noise Augmentation Improves Non-Invasive Brain-to-Speech
summary: Non-invasive brain-to-speech decoding aims to restore communication to patients suffering from neurodegenerative disease, without the risks of neurosurgery. Existing MEG- and EEG-based methods, while scalable, continue to suffer from high word error rates driven by relatively low signal-to-noise ratios compared to invasive recordings. We propose physiological noise augmentation (PNA), a data augmentation method that explicitly trains decoders to become invariant to task-agnostic artifacts (e.g. ocular and cardiac activity). PNA draws inspiration from automatic speech recognition systems, where environmental noise (e.g. dogs barking, city traffic) is added to clean speech to improve robustness. Analogously, we decompose brain recordings into clean data and noise artifacts using independent component analysis (ICA), before scaling and remixing to generate biophysically realistic, label-preserving training examples. We show that PNA approximates anisotropic regularization, penalizing decoder sensitivity along artifact-dominated directions. On MegNIST, a 12k-trial imagined-digit MEG dataset, PNA with 10-trial averaging improves EEGNet decoding accuracy by 4.7 percentage points (absolute) over training on real data alone. Our results suggest that artifact-aware augmentation and trial averaging are complementary tools for improving robustness in non-invasive speech BCIs.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes Physiological Noise Augmentation (PNA), a data augmentation method that improves non-invasive brain-to-speech decoding by training decoders to become invariant to task-agnostic artifacts (e.g., ocular and cardiac activity) via ICA-based decomposition and remixing of noise, achieving 4.7% accuracy improvement on the MegNIST dataset.
AI.motivation: Existing MEG- and EEG-based brain-to-speech decoding methods suffer from high word error rates due to low signal-to-noise ratios compared to invasive recordings, motivating the need for robustness against physiological artifacts without requiring neurosurgery.
AI.method: PNA decomposes brain recordings into clean data and noise artifacts using ICA, then scales and remixes them to generate biophysically realistic, label-preserving training examples, drawing inspiration from environmental noise augmentation in automatic speech recognition.
AI.result: On the MegNIST dataset (12k-trial imagined-digit MEG), PNA with 10-trial averaging improves EEGNet decoding accuracy by 4.7 percentage points (absolute) over training on real data alone.
AI.conclusion: Artifact-aware augmentation (PNA) and trial averaging are complementary tools for improving robustness in non-invasive speech brain-computer interfaces.

title: Framework and Multi-modal Dataset for Roadwork Zone Detection and Geo-localization
comment: Accepted to IEEE IV25. The RZDG dataset and code can be found at: https://github.com/chrisyan/RZDG
summary: Autonomous vehicles often rely on high-definition (HD) maps for navigation; however, these maps are not frequently updated and often lack semi-static information, such as temporary roadwork zones, which can significantly alter the road network. This limitation underscores the urgent need for an accurate global position of roadwork zones. However, the absence of publicly available datasets for evaluating roadwork zone detection and geo-localization models has hindered the development of reliable autonomous driving systems. To address this challenge, we propose the Roadwork Zone Detection and Geo-localization (RZDG) dataset, which includes both simulated and real-world data, providing multimodal sensor inputs along with comprehensive annotations. The dataset supports multiple perception tasks, including image semantic segmentation, 3D object detection, and object geo-localization. In addition, we introduce a tracker-based roadwork zone detection and geo-localization (RZDG) pipeline, an extension of AB3DMOT, for accurate object geo-localization in roadwork zones. We benchmark our approach on the RZDG dataset, demonstrating its effectiveness in detecting roadwork zones and transforming object positions from the local coordinate system to the global coordinate system. A prediction is considered a true positive (TP) if its estimated position falls within one meter of the ground truth. Our experimental results show that our approach achieves high accuracy on both real and simulated data. Specifically, we report: Precision: 0.565 (real) / 0.615 (simulated) Recall: 0.898 (real) / 0.809 (simulated) F1-score: 0.597 (real) / 0.665 (simulated).

AI.tldr: The paper introduces the RZDG dataset (simulated + real-world multimodal data) for detecting and geo-localizing roadwork zones, along with a tracker-based pipeline (extension of AB3DMOT) that achieves moderate precision but high recall in transforming object positions to global coordinates.
AI.motivation: HD maps lack semi-static roadwork zone information, and no public dataset exists for evaluating roadwork zone detection and geo-localization, hindering reliable autonomous driving development.
AI.method: Proposes the RZDG dataset (multimodal, annotated for semantic segmentation, 3D object detection, geo-localization) and a tracker-based pipeline extending AB3DMOT for roadwork zone detection and geo-localization.
AI.result: Precision: 0.565 (real) / 0.615 (simulated); Recall: 0.898 (real) / 0.809 (simulated); F1-score: 0.597 (real) / 0.665 (simulated), with TP defined as estimated position within 1 meter of ground truth.
AI.conclusion: The approach achieves high accuracy in detecting and geo-localizing roadwork zones on both real and simulated data, demonstrating effectiveness for autonomous driving systems.

title: MeGA-MP: Metric Graph Advection Message Passing -- A Physics-Informed Message Passing Operator for Advection-Dominated Metric Graphs
summary: Many real-world systems are organized as networks where spatio-temporal dynamics unfold along connections and not discretely between nodes. Examples include utility networks such as water distribution systems or gas networks, electrical grids, and traffic flow networks. Such systems are naturally modeled as metric graphs, where edges correspond to one-dimensional Euclidean subspaces connected at vertices. Metric graphs are independent of an underlying global Euclidean space, limiting direct application of typical PINNs and operator-learning methods. Especially transport dynamics like advection require a methodology able to capture antisymmetric and long-range dependencies on graphs, which is itself a challenge. We propose a novel physics-informed message passing operator that encodes linear advection on metric graphs as an inductive bias. In the purely advective setting, the operator provably recovers the exact dynamics up to a theoretically derived discretization error without any training. Combined with trainable components like MLPs, our message passing operator extends to realistic advection-reaction dynamics in water distribution systems, where we achieve superior performance compared to baselines and zero-shot generalization across different graph topologies.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a physics-informed message passing operator that encodes linear advection on metric graphs as an inductive bias, achieving provably exact dynamics recovery without training in purely advective settings and superior performance for advection-reaction dynamics in water distribution systems with zero-shot generalization across graph topologies.
AI.motivation: Real-world systems like water distribution, gas networks, electrical grids, and traffic flow are organized as networks where spatio-temporal dynamics unfold along connections (edges) rather than discretely between nodes. These systems are naturally modeled as metric graphs, but standard PINNs and operator-learning methods cannot be directly applied due to the lack of an underlying global Euclidean space. Additionally, transport dynamics like advection require capturing antisymmetric and long-range dependencies on graphs.
AI.method: A novel physics-informed message passing operator that encodes linear advection on metric graphs as an inductive bias. The method provably recovers exact dynamics up to a theoretically derived discretization error without any training in the purely advective setting. For realistic advection-reaction dynamics, trainable components like MLPs are combined with the message passing operator.
AI.result: In purely advective settings, the operator provably recovers exact dynamics without training. For advection-reaction dynamics in water distribution systems, the method achieves superior performance compared to baselines and demonstrates zero-shot generalization across different graph topologies.
AI.conclusion: The physics-informed message passing operator effectively handles advection dynamics on metric graphs, outperforming baselines and generalizing to unseen graph topologies without retraining, making it suitable for real-world network systems with spatio-temporal dynamics along connections.

title: IRIS: An Intelligent Vision-Language System for Ocular Surface Diseases via Topic Tree and Scene-Driven VQA Generation
summary: While Large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) demonstrate remarkable generic capabilities, their clinical reasoning in specialized domains like ocular surface diseases (OSDs) is severely hindered by a paucity of high-fidelity, multimodal instruction-tuning data. To dismantle this data bottleneck, we introduce IRIS, an Intelligent Recognition and Interaction System tailored for fine-grained OSD understanding via external eye photography. First, we curate IRIS-120K, the largest and most comprehensive OSD visual question-answering (VQA) dataset to date. Crucially, to overcome the semantic shallowness of conventional image-caption pairs, we propose a synergistic data generation paradigm to explicitly inject clinical priors. Our data engine operates via a dual-branch framework: 1) a Topic Finding Tree (TFT) that hierarchically anchors visual features to precise anatomical and pathological concepts, enforcing rigorous medical deduction logic; and 2) a Scene-driven strategy that synthesizes role-adaptive clinical dialogues to ensure pragmatic generalization. By explicitly aligning a compact 4B-parameter VLM on this structurally enriched corpus, IRIS achieves state-of-the-art performance, comprehensively outperforming both generalist and specialized medical VLMs with up to 34B parameters. Our findings underscore that structured knowledge injection profoundly prevails over sheer parameter scaling, unlocking the potential for resource-efficient, expert-level AI deployment on mobile edge devices for scalable OSD screening. Code, datasets, and model weights will be publicly released by this repo.

AI.tldr: IRIS introduces a dual-branch data generation framework (Topic Finding Tree + Scene-driven strategy) to create the IRIS-120K OSD VQA dataset, and by fine-tuning a compact 4B-parameter VLM on this structured knowledge-injected corpus, achieves state-of-the-art performance surpassing larger models up to 34B parameters for ocular surface disease understanding.
AI.motivation: Large VLMs fail at clinical reasoning for ocular surface diseases (OSDs) due to a lack of high-fidelity, multimodal instruction-tuning data with sufficient clinical depth, creating a data bottleneck that prevents expert-level domain-specific understanding.
AI.method: A dual-branch synergistic data generation paradigm: (1) Topic Finding Tree (TFT) hierarchically anchors visual features to anatomical/pathological concepts with rigorous medical deduction logic; (2) Scene-driven strategy synthesizes role-adaptive clinical dialogues for pragmatic generalization. A 4B-parameter VLM is fine-tuned on the resulting IRIS-120K dataset.
AI.result: IRIS with 4B parameters achieves state-of-the-art performance on OSD understanding, comprehensively outperforming both generalist and specialized medical VLMs with up to 34B parameters, demonstrating that structured knowledge injection prevails over sheer parameter scaling.
AI.conclusion: Structured clinical knowledge injection is more effective than model scaling for domain-specific medical VLM performance, enabling resource-efficient, expert-level AI deployment on mobile edge devices for scalable OSD screening.

title: Platonic Projection Structures: Operator-Induced Observability in Representation Learning
summary: We characterize observability in representation learning through Platonic Projection Structures (PPS), an operator-theoretic framework for analyzing representation accessibility under partial observation. Rather than treating observable outputs as direct reflections of latent representations, PPS models observation through a self-adjoint positive semidefinite operator acting on a latent representation space.
