A system is represented as a triple $(H, Π, O)$, where $H$ is a latent representation space, $Π\succeq 0$ is an observation operator, and $O(v)=\langle v,Πv\rangle$ defines an induced scalar observable. Observability is characterized by the quotient geometry $H/\ker(Π)$, representing equivalence classes of latent states indistinguishable under observation. We show that quantum measurement and representation inference under linear observation models share this operator-theoretic structure while differing in the algebraic properties of their observation operators; the correspondence is structural rather than physical. Representation transfer and knowledge distillation can likewise be interpreted as approximate preservation of observable geometry through $ΦΠ_T \approx Π_S Φ$. PPS also reveals a structural limitation of output-based interpretability: latent components in $\ker(Π)$ are inaccessible from induced observables, imposing intrinsic constraints on attribution and explanation methods. Controlled empirical validations demonstrate kernel-invariant observability, projection-induced attribution gaps, and rank-controlled observable geometry in latent representation spaces. PPS thus provides an explicit characterization of observability through operator-induced quotient geometry and a unified perspective on representation accessibility, interpretability, and projection-mediated inference.

AI.tldr: PPS is an operator-theoretic framework using self-adjoint positive semidefinite observation operators to characterize observability in representation learning via quotient geometry $H/\ker(\Pi)$, showing that latent components in $\ker(\Pi)$ are inaccessible, with applications to quantum measurement, knowledge distillation, and interpretability limitations.
AI.motivation: Observable outputs do not directly reflect latent representations under partial observation; there is no unified framework to characterize what can and cannot be observed about latent representations. PPS formalizes this gap.
AI.method: Models observation as a triple $(H, \Pi, O)$ where $\Pi\succeq 0$ is a self-adjoint positive semidefinite observation operator on latent space $H$, and $O(v)=\langle v,\Pi v\rangle$ defines induced scalar observables. Observability is characterized via quotient geometry $H/\ker(\Pi)$. Representation transfer is formalized as $\Phi\Pi_T \approx \Pi_S \Phi$.
AI.result: Empirical validations show kernel-invariant observability, projection-induced attribution gaps, and rank-controlled observable geometry. PPS reveals that quantum measurement and linear representation inference share the same operator-theoretic structure but differ in algebraic operator properties.
AI.conclusion: PPS provides an explicit characterization of observability through operator-induced quotient geometry and a unified perspective on representation accessibility, interpretability, and projection-mediated inference, while exposing fundamental limitations of output-based interpretability methods.

title: Last-Meter Precision Navigation for UAVs: A Diffusion-Refined Aerial Visual Servoing Approach
summary: In this work, we study the last-meter precision navigation for UAVs, e.g., autonomously reaching a target within the final 10 meters using monocular vision. This task is challenging due to scale ambiguity, rotation discontinuities, and the need for fine-grained spatial reasoning. Existing methods often fail under large viewpoint changes or lack generalization to unseen environments. To this end, we propose DreamNav, a coarse-to-fine diffusion-refined aerial visual servoing framework. In the first coarse-estimation stage, a robust regression policy employs a trigonometric parameterization to predict rotation by jointly modeling sine and cosine components, effectively mitigating optimization instabilities caused by angular periodicity. Given this coarse estimate, the second diffusion-refined stage utilizes a pre-trained world model to simulate future visual observations for candidate actions, selecting the trajectory that minimizes visual discrepancy with the target through a process of visual imagination. To support rigorous evaluation, we contribute PairUAV, a large-scale benchmark comprising 4.8 million image pairs across 72 scenes, curated from the University-1652 dataset. Extensive experiments show DreamNav outperforms strong visual servoing and foundation model baselines in accuracy and generalization, with zero-shot transfer to unseen scenes.

AI.tldr: DreamNav is a coarse-to-fine diffusion-refined aerial visual servoing framework for UAV last-meter precision navigation. It uses a trigonometric regression policy for coarse rotation estimation and a diffusion-based world model for fine-grained trajectory refinement via visual imagination. The paper also introduces PairUAV, a large-scale benchmark of 4.8M image pairs across 72 scenes. DreamNav achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and zero-shot generalization.
AI.motivation: Last-meter precision navigation for UAVs (within 10m) using monocular vision is challenging due to scale ambiguity, rotation discontinuities, and poor generalization of existing methods under large viewpoint changes.
AI.method: A coarse-to-fine pipeline: (1) Coarse stage uses a robust regression policy with trigonometric parameterization (joint sine/cosine modeling) to predict rotation; (2) Fine stage employs a pre-trained diffusion world model to simulate future visual observations, selecting trajectories that minimize visual discrepancy with the target.
AI.result: Outperforms strong visual servoing and foundation model baselines in accuracy and generalization; demonstrates zero-shot transfer to unseen scenes. The PairUAV benchmark contains 4.8M image pairs across 72 scenes.
AI.conclusion: DreamNav effectively addresses scale ambiguity and rotation discontinuities in UAV last-meter navigation, achieving robust zero-shot generalization through coarse-to-fine diffusion refinement.

title: Relational Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Pricing in High-Speed Railway Markets
summary: In liberalised railway systems, operators must set prices dynamically in an environment with partial observability, as they retain private information about their objectives and performance, where regulatory constraints prohibit communication or direct information exchange between competitors to prevent explicit collusion. Consequently, agents must learn to infer strategic interactions only from observable market data which presents a significant challenge for multi-agent reinforcement learning, where standard approaches typically treat observations as unstructured vectors, ignoring the underlying market topology that governs strategic interactions. To address this, an entity graph modelling approach is proposed, which represents the environment as a graph of operational units, rather than decision-making agents or static infrastructure, encoding competition, coordination, and connectivity relations between entities. Then, an extension of the multi-agent twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm with graph-based representation learning processes the features of the entities through a multi-layer relational graph convolutional network and aggregates them via a learnt attention mechanism. Experimental results in a rail pricing reinforcement learning environment show that this novel framework achieves higher revenue and stability in two different settings of increasing market complexity compared to a representative selection of relational and non-relational baselines. The code is publicly available at: https://github.com/Kinrre/RelationalRailPricing-RL

AI.tldr: A graph-based multi-agent reinforcement learning framework using entity graph modelling and relational graph convolutional networks (R-GCN) with attention mechanisms is proposed for dynamic pricing in liberalised railway systems, outperforming baselines in revenue and stability under partial observability and regulatory constraints.
AI.motivation: In liberalised railway systems, operators must set prices dynamically under partial observability with private information and regulatory constraints that prohibit direct communication. Standard multi-agent reinforcement learning approaches treat observations as unstructured vectors, ignoring the underlying market topology that governs strategic interactions, making learning to infer competitive dynamics from observable market data a significant challenge.
AI.method: The authors propose an entity graph modelling approach representing the environment as a graph of operational units (encoding competition, coordination, and connectivity relations), and extend the multi-agent twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (MATD3) algorithm with graph-based representation learning. Features are processed through a multi-layer relational graph convolutional network (R-GCN) and aggregated via a learnt attention mechanism.
AI.result: In a rail pricing reinforcement learning environment, the proposed framework achieves higher revenue and stability in two settings of increasing market complexity compared to a selection of relational and non-relational baselines.
AI.conclusion: The graph-structured representation of market topology enables more effective multi-agent learning under partial observability and communication constraints, outperforming standard approaches that ignore relational structure.

title: HASSL: Hierarchy-Aware Self-Supervised Learning Framework for Single Cell Microscopy
summary: Hierarchical structure is common in image data, where fine-grained clusters often merge into larger, coarser semantic groups. In biological cell images, current self-supervised learning models often suppress this hierarchy, as coarse factors such as imaging modality can obscure finer morphological attributes in the latent space. We propose a hierarchy-aware self-supervised training framework to address this problem. Our method combines two components: a distillation framework with a segmentation teacher to improve morphological awareness in the latent space, and a hierarchy-aware contrastive loss based on HDBSCAN to improve decision boundaries between closely related subtypes at different hierarchical levels. Together, these components reduce the tendency of self-supervised learning to overemphasize coarse factors and instead align embeddings with semantic and morphological cues. This yields biologically meaningful sub-clusters driven by fine morphological detail. We train and evaluate our method on a curated corpus of 2.3 million single cells aggregated from 20 microscopy datasets, both labeled and unlabeled, covering 208 cell classes. Our method improves over baseline and counterpart methods, increasing average top-K accuracy by 2.8%, top-9 retrieval on the dataset with the deepest hierarchy by 6.3%, and downstream F1-score for biologically relevant drug classification from perturbed cell morphology by 7.8%.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a hierarchy-aware self-supervised learning framework for cell image analysis that uses a distillation framework with a segmentation teacher and HDBSCAN-based contrastive loss to improve morphological awareness and decision boundaries across hierarchical levels, achieving improvements in top-K accuracy, retrieval, and drug classification F1-score on a large multi-dataset corpus of 2.3 million single cells across 208 classes.
AI.motivation: Self-supervised learning models often suppress hierarchical structure in cell images, as coarse factors like imaging modality dominate the latent space and obscure fine-grained morphological attributes, making it difficult to distinguish biologically meaningful sub-clusters.
AI.method: The framework combines (1) a distillation framework with a segmentation teacher to enhance morphological awareness in the latent space, and (2) a hierarchy-aware contrastive loss based on HDBSCAN clustering to refine decision boundaries between related subtypes at different hierarchical levels.
AI.result: On a corpus of 2.3 million single cells from 20 microscopy datasets (208 classes), the method improves average top-K accuracy by 2.8%, top-9 retrieval on the deepest hierarchy dataset by 6.3%, and downstream F1-score for drug classification from perturbed cell morphology by 7.8%.
AI.conclusion: The proposed hierarchy-aware training framework reduces self-supervised learning's tendency to overemphasize coarse factors and better aligns embeddings with semantic and morphological cues, yielding biologically meaningful sub-clusters driven by fine morphological detail.

title: SMART: A Machine Learning and Monte Carlo Framework for Rapid Analysis of Stochastic Transistor Aging and Process Variation in Digital Circuits
comment: Submitted to Engineering Reports, Under Review
summary: As CMOS technology scales into the deep nanometer regime, digital circuit reliability is increasingly threatened by the combined stochastic effects of Bias Temperature Instability (BTI) and Process Variation (PV). Traditional reliability analysis methods, which rely on computationally intensive simulations or extensive lookup tables, fail to scale efficiently for large designs, creating a critical bottleneck in design space exploration. To address this, we propose SMART, a novel framework that integrates Machine Learning (ML) with Monte Carlo simulation to enable rapid, high-fidelity reliability analysis. SMART employs Random Forest regression to predict gate delay distributions directly, bypassing time-consuming atomic model parameter extractions. Crucially, the model utilizes Bayesian Optimization for automated hyperparameter tuning, ensuring maximum predictive robustness across diverse libraries. Experimental validation on ISCAS85 benchmark circuits demonstrates that SMART achieves a 94.54% reduction in analysis time compared to state-of-the-art methods, while maintaining a remarkable average accuracy error of just 1.63%. By shifting computational complexity to an offline training phase, the proposed framework offers a scalable, accurate solution for designing resilient, reliability-aware digital systems.

AI.tldr: SMART is an ML-Monte Carlo hybrid framework using Random Forest regression with Bayesian optimization to predict gate delay distributions, achieving 94.54% faster reliability analysis with only 1.63% accuracy error compared to traditional methods.
AI.motivation: Traditional reliability analysis methods for BTI and PV effects rely on computationally intensive simulations or extensive lookup tables, which fail to scale efficiently for large digital circuit designs in the deep nanometer CMOS regime.
AI.method: SMART integrates Machine Learning (Random Forest regression) with Monte Carlo simulation, employs Bayesian Optimization for automated hyperparameter tuning, and shifts computational complexity to an offline training phase to predict gate delay distributions directly without atomic model parameter extractions.
AI.result: Achieves 94.54% reduction in analysis time compared to state-of-the-art methods with an average accuracy error of 1.63%, validated on ISCAS85 benchmark circuits.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework offers a scalable, accurate solution for designing resilient, reliability-aware digital systems by enabling rapid, high-fidelity reliability analysis.

title: Event Detection in Videos: A Framework for the Development of New Methods
summary:
Event detection tasks in videos, the most important aspect of video surveillance, aim to detect events either at the pixel-level, frame-level, or clip-level. Plenty of methods intended for event detection in different environments, for various applications, and within different acquisition techniques were introduced. Naturally, the attempts were made as well to classify these algorithms in terms of detection of performance or in terms of real-time abilities. Nevertheless, the lack of a large-scale dataset as well as rigorous performance evaluation methods have biased such comparisons as well as the development of the methods.
  Given the diversity of existing approaches, we believe it is essential for researchers to position their work within such a rich landscape. Thus, we propose a rigorous framework for developing new methods in event detection for videos. Specifically, this framework is based on three main pillars: datasets, performance evaluation, and scenarios for deploying methods.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a rigorous framework for event detection in videos, structured around three pillars: datasets, performance evaluation, and deployment scenarios, addressing the lack of standardized benchmarks and evaluation methods in the field.
AI.motivation: The lack of large-scale datasets and rigorous performance evaluation methods has biased comparisons between event detection algorithms and hindered method development. A standardized framework is needed to help researchers position their work within the diverse landscape of existing approaches.
AI.method: The proposed framework is built on three main pillars: (1) datasets, (2) performance evaluation, and (3) scenarios for deploying methods, providing a structured approach for developing and comparing event detection methods in videos.
AI.result: A rigorous framework for developing new methods in event detection for videos, addressing the diversity of existing approaches and enabling researchers to benchmark their work systematically.
AI.conclusion: Establishing a standardized framework with clear datasets, evaluation metrics, and deployment scenarios is essential for advancing video event detection research and enabling fair comparisons across methods.

title: The Good, the Bad, and the Brittle: Benchmarking Robustness and Generalisation of Histopathology Foundation Models
summary: How robust and generalisable are pathology foundation models and have their scaling limites been reached? We benchmarked twelve pathology foundation models (PFMs) and ResNet baselines using our Robustness Evaluation and Enhancement Toolbox (REET) across eleven clinically realistic perturbations and a dissimilarity-driven Non-Redundant K-fold validation (NR-Kfold) protocol. We introduce a Perturbation Performance Index (PPI) to summarise accuracy trends under controlled perturbation sweeps and analyse robustness scaling with parameter count. We show that PFMs consistently outperform CNNs in both robustness and domain generalisation, yet model scaling shows diminishing returns: mid-sized models such (UNI2/Virchow-2 etc.) achieve comparable or greater resilience than larger systems. NR-Kfold analysis further reveals systematic accuracy loss and increased variability when training-test similarity is broken, underscoring the need for explicit distribution-shift evaluation. These findings suggest that the next generation of pathology foundation models must prioritise data quality, multimodality information and domain alignment over parameter count to achieve genuine clinical reliability.

AI.tldr: Benchmarking 12 pathology foundation models (PFMs) against ResNets using a robustness toolbox (REET) with 11 perturbations and NR-Kfold validation shows PFMs outperform CNNs in robustness and generalisation, but scaling exhibits diminishing returns, with mid-sized models often matching larger ones. Results indicate future PFMs should prioritise data quality and domain alignment over parameter count.
AI.motivation: To assess the robustness, generalisability, and scaling limits of current pathology foundation models, given their increasing adoption in clinical settings where distribution shifts are common.
AI.method: Evaluated 12 PFMs and ResNet baselines using the REET toolbox across 11 clinically realistic perturbations and a dissimilarity-driven Non-Redundant K-fold (NR-Kfold) validation protocol. Introduced the Perturbation Performance Index (PPI) to summarise accuracy under controlled perturbation sweeps and analysed robustness scaling with model parameter count.
AI.result: PFMs consistently outperform CNNs in robustness and domain generalisation. However, model scaling shows diminishing returns: mid-sized models (e.g., UNI2, Virchow-2) achieve comparable or greater resilience than larger systems. NR-Kfold reveals systematic accuracy loss and increased variability when training-test similarity is broken.
AI.conclusion: Next-generation pathology foundation models should prioritise data quality, multimodality information, and domain alignment over parameter count to achieve genuine clinical reliability.

title: Noisy-Channel Minimum Bayes Risk Decoding
summary: Minimum Bayes Risk (MBR) decoding yields more robust and higher-quality text generation than maximum a posteriori (MAP) decoding by selecting hypotheses that maximize expected utility over sampled pseudo-references. However, there exists a discrepancy in the design: hypothesis selection calculates expected utility scores conditioned on given pseudo-references, while commonly used evaluation metrics, e.g., BLEU and COMET, are asymmetric. Therefore, it is important to consider both hypothesis-to-reference and reference-to-hypothesis directional effects. In this study, we introduce a noisy channel decomposition of MBR decoding that naturally incorporates bidirectional effects to account for these asymmetries. We decompose MBR decoding into four interacting components: hypothesis-to-reference likelihood, reference-to-hypothesis likelihood, hypothesis prior, and reference prior. This decomposition provides a unified interpretation of existing MBR variants and enables metric- and task-specific interpretability by isolating the contribution of each channel. Our comprehensive analysis reveals that channel-wise contributions exhibit distinct characteristics across metrics while remaining consistent across tasks, and suggests that appropriate channel weighting may lead to improvements over original MBR decoding.

AI.tldr: MBR decoding suffers from asymmetry between hypothesis selection and evaluation metrics. This paper introduces a noisy channel decomposition of MBR that incorporates bidirectional effects (hypothesis-to-reference and reference-to-hypothesis), decomposing MBR into four components: two likelihoods and two priors. Analysis shows distinct channel characteristics across metrics but consistency across tasks, with potential improvements via channel weighting.
AI.motivation: Existing MBR decoding uses asymmetric evaluation metrics (e.g., BLEU, COMET) that only measure hypothesis-to-reference, creating a discrepancy with the symmetric expectation framework. The authors aim to address this mismatch by incorporating bidirectional effects.
AI.method: The authors propose a noisy channel decomposition of MBR decoding that splits the expected utility into four components: hypothesis-to-reference likelihood, reference-to-hypothesis likelihood, hypothesis prior, and reference prior. This framework unifies existing MBR variants and allows per-component analysis.
AI.result: Channel-wise contributions show distinct characteristics depending on the metric used (e.g., BLEU vs. COMET), but these characteristics remain consistent across different text generation tasks. Appropriate weighting of channels may improve upon standard MBR decoding.
AI.conclusion: The noisy channel decomposition provides a unified interpretation of MBR variants and enables metric- and task-specific interpretability. The analysis suggests potential gains from adaptive channel weighting, addressing the asymmetry issue in MBR decoding.

title: Transferability Between Understanding and Generation in Unified Multimodal Models
comment: Accepted at ECCV 2026. Project Page: this https URL
summary: Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) integrate image understanding and generation within a single architecture, yet how the two tasks interact remains understudied. We investigate $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{transferability}}$ in UMMs: whether training a capability on one task improves the same capability on the other without explicit supervision. Through controlled experiments, we empirically find that transferability depends on architecture-models with fully shared transformer backbone and a unified visual encoder exhibit consistent cross-task transfer, while loosely coupled designs show little or none. Leveraging this transferability, we propose a practical training strategy. The most straightforward way to improve a target generative capability (e.g., counting) is to fine-tune generation directly, but this can degrade visual quality due to distribution shift. Instead, we train the corresponding understanding task and let it transfer into generation, which improves capability-specific generative performance while minimizing distribution shift. We validate this across three capabilities-counting, spatial relation, and text recognition/generation-showing that cross-task transferability can be systematically exploited in UMMs.

AI.tldr: Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) show that cross-task transferability (e.g., training understanding improves generation) depends on architecture—fully shared backbones enable it, loosely coupled designs do not. Exploiting this, training understanding tasks instead of generation avoids distribution shift and improves generative capabilities like counting, spatial relations, and text recognition.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether and how cross-task transferability (training one capability on one task improving the same capability on the other) occurs in Unified Multimodal Models, and to leverage this phenomenon for more effective training.
AI.method: Controlled experiments comparing architecture designs (fully shared transformer backbone + unified visual encoder vs. loosely coupled designs) for cross-task transfer; a training strategy that trains understanding tasks and lets the capability transfer to generation, avoiding direct fine-tuning on generation.
AI.result: Transferability is architecture-dependent—fully shared backbones exhibit consistent cross-task transfer while loosely coupled models show little to none. Training understanding tasks improves generative performance for counting, spatial relations, and text recognition/generation while minimizing visual quality degradation from distribution shift.
AI.conclusion: Cross-task transferability exists in UMMs under appropriate architectural conditions and can be systematically exploited to improve generative capabilities without the distribution shift caused by direct generation fine-tuning.

title: FlatManifold: Robust Continual Learning under Severe Label Noise and Domain Shifts via Intrinsic Manifold Flattening
summary:
In non-stationary streaming environments, simultaneously adapting to complex, non-linear domain shifts via continual learning while mitigating the catastrophic effects of severe, uncalibrated label noise poses a fundamental mathematical challenge. In this paper, we propose \FlatManifold{}, a novel, streamlined robust continual learning framework that utilizes a Nyström manifold flattening map based on the kernel trick and projection onto an orthogonalized Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS).
  Unlike traditional methods that rely on complex, error-prone sample-filtering pipelines, the proposed approach exploits the intrinsic mathematical robustness of the flattened space itself. By mapping feature distributions onto a fixed orthogonal target topology with a ridge regularizer, the framework naturally smoothes and counteracts the influence of extreme label noise during the optimization process. Concurrently, catastrophic forgetting is prevented via a continual topology brake term that leverages the covariance matrix of past experiences.
  Extensive evaluation on real-world multi-session robotics datasets demonstrates that even under severe conditions featuring 40\% symmetric label noise, \FlatManifold{} successfully mitigates gradient corruption. Under extreme cross-session domain shifts spanning various seasons and lighting conditions, the proposed framework establishes high generalization capabilities, significantly outperforming standard sequential optimization baselines and proving that structural linearization itself serves as a powerful mathematical barrier against distributed label corruption.

AI.tldr: FlatManifold is a robust continual learning framework that uses a Nyström manifold flattening map and orthogonalized RKHS projection to simultaneously handle non-stationary domain shifts and severe label noise (up to 40% symmetric noise), outperforming baselines on real-world robotics datasets.
AI.motivation: To address the dual challenge of adapting to non-linear domain shifts in non-stationary streaming environments while mitigating catastrophic effects of severe, uncalibrated label noise.
AI.method: Proposes FlatManifold, which uses a Nyström manifold flattening map based on the kernel trick and projection onto an orthogonalized RKHS. It employs a ridge regularizer for noise robustness and a continual topology brake term using past covariance matrices to prevent catastrophic forgetting.
AI.result: On real-world multi-session robotics datasets with 40% symmetric label noise and extreme cross-session domain shifts, FlatManifold successfully mitigates gradient corruption and establishes high generalization, significantly outperforming sequential optimization baselines.
AI.conclusion: Structural linearization via manifold flattening serves as a powerful mathematical barrier against distributed label corruption, proving that intrinsic robustness of the flattened space is more effective than complex sample-filtering pipelines.

title: Video-based detection of cessation of breathing in pre-term infants using machine learning
comment: Paper submitted to Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine (CMPB)
summary:
Pre-term infants are susceptible to potentially harmful apnoea-related cessations of breathing due to immature respiratory control. However, reliable respiratory monitoring in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) remains challenging because motion artefacts, sensor displacement, and skin fragility can compromise contact-based measurements. Non-contact video monitoring offers a complementary approach that does not depend on adhesive sensors while providing additional respiratory information.
  We investigated whether camera-based signals can detect apnoea-related cessation of breathing (COBE) and provide complementary information to routinely acquired physiological signals. Using video and clinical recordings from 30 pre-term infants, respiratory motion was extracted from dynamically tracked torso regions to generate camera-derived time-series signals. Camera-only models were trained using residual network (ResNet) architectures, while hybrid models combined video-derived signals with impedance pneumography (IP), ECG-derived respiration (EDR), and the PPG-derived respiratory envelope.
  Camera-only models achieved a balanced accuracy of 76.9%, demonstrating the feasibility of non-contact COBE detection. Combining video-derived features with IP improved balanced accuracy to 90.6%, outperforming either modality alone and indicating that video provides respiratory information beyond standard physiological signals.
  These findings show that video-derived signals contain clinically relevant respiratory features and enhance COBE detection when combined with conventional physiological signals. This supports non-contact video as a complementary modality for automated COBE detection and highlights its potential to improve the robustness of neonatal respiratory monitoring.

AI.tldr: Camera-based non-contact monitoring can detect apnoea-related breathing cessations in pre-term infants, achieving 76.9% balanced accuracy with video-only models and 90.6% when combined with impedance pneumography, demonstrating its value as a complementary modality to conventional physiological signals in the NICU.
AI.motivation: Pre-term infants are vulnerable to apnoea-related breathing cessations due to immature respiratory control, but existing contact-based monitoring in the NICU is compromised by motion artefacts, sensor displacement, and skin fragility. Non-contact video monitoring offers a potential solution that avoids these limitations.
AI.method: Respiratory motion was extracted from dynamically tracked torso regions of 30 pre-term infants using video recordings. Camera-only models were trained with ResNet architectures, and hybrid models combined video-derived signals with impedance pneumography (IP), ECG-derived respiration (EDR), and PPG-derived respiratory envelope.
AI.result: Camera-only models achieved 76.9% balanced accuracy for detecting cessation of breathing (COBE). Hybrid models combining video features with IP achieved 90.6% balanced accuracy, outperforming either modality alone.
AI.conclusion: Video-derived signals contain clinically relevant respiratory features that enhance COBE detection when combined with conventional signals, supporting non-contact video as a complementary modality for automated apnoea detection and improved neonatal respiratory monitoring robustness.

title: CanniUplift: A Holistic Framework for Mitigating Seller and Incentive Cannibalization in E-commerce Uplift Modeling
summary: Personalized incentive allocation is vital for e-commerce, where uplift modeling is the standard for estimating Individual Treatment Effects (ITE). However, traditional models often fail in complex multi-seller environments with violations of the Stable Unit Treatment Value Assumption (SUTVA). We identify two critical challenges: Seller-level Cannibalization, where incentives shift expenditure between shops without growing the platform, and Incentive-level Cannibalization, where organic conversions or alternative rewards introduce significant noise into incrementality estimation. In this paper, we propose CanniUplift, a unified framework to mitigate these dual-source cannibalization effects. Specifically, we design Platform-level Global Alignment (PGA) to capture cross-shop substitution through global GMV consistency constraints. To tackle incentive-driven noise, we introduce Redemption-based Decomposition Denoising (RDD), which uses redemption behavior to decompose treated outcomes and reduce attribution noise within an entire-space framework. Furthermore, a Treat-Attention mechanism is designed to model intricate interactions between users' historical behaviors and current treatment options. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and large-scale industrial datasets demonstrate that CanniUplift significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Ablation studies confirm that the integration of PGA and RDD consistently improves wAUUC and wQINI. Successfully deployed online, our framework achieved a 4.08% relative increase in platform-wide incremental GMV (Delta GMV) over the production baseline and improved ROI in online A/B tests, proving effective in driving global platform growth.

AI.tldr: CanniUplift is a unified framework that mitigates dual-source cannibalization effects (seller-level and incentive-level) in uplift modeling for e-commerce incentive allocation, using Platform-level Global Alignment (PGA) and Redemption-based Decomposition Denoising (RDD), achieving significant improvements in wAUUC, wQINI, and a 4.08% relative increase in platform-wide incremental GMV in online deployment.
AI.motivation: Traditional uplift models fail in complex multi-seller e-commerce environments due to SUTVA violations, specifically Seller-level Cannibalization (incentives shift expenditure between shops without platform growth) and Incentive-level Cannibalization (organic conversions or alternative rewards introduce noise into incrementality estimation).
AI.method: Proposes CanniUplift with three components: (1) Platform-level Global Alignment (PGA) to capture cross-shop substitution via global GMV consistency constraints; (2) Redemption-based Decomposition Denoising (RDD) using redemption behavior to decompose treated outcomes within an entire-space framework; (3) Treat-Attention mechanism to model interactions between users' historical behaviors and current treatment options.
AI.result: Outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on synthetic and large-scale industrial datasets; ablation studies confirm PGA and RDD consistently improve wAUUC and wQINI; online deployment yields 4.08% relative increase in platform-wide incremental GMV and improved ROI.
AI.conclusion: CanniUplift effectively addresses dual-source cannibalization in multi-seller e-commerce, proving effective in driving global platform growth both offline and online.

title: Fields of the Planet: Field Boundary Mapping Beyond 10m
summary: Field-boundary maps support crop monitoring, irrigation planning, and yield estimation, but many smallholder parcels span only a few 10 m Sentinel-2 pixels. We introduce Fields of the Planet (FTP), a 3 m PlanetScope companion to Fields of The World (FTW) that pairs the same polygons, seasonal windows, and train/test splits with 133,168 co-registered PlanetScope patch-window targets across 24 countries. FTP evaluates field delineation as parcel recovery by vectorizing predictions before scoring panoptic quality (PQ), object F1, size-stratified PQ, and meter-scale matched-boundary error. Under matched architectures and training recipes, 3 m imagery raises PQ from 21.0 to 35.5, raises PQ on sub-0.5 ha fields from 5.8 to 15.7, and cuts matched-boundary error from 18.6 m to 7.4 m.

AI.tldr: A dataset (FTP) of 3 m PlanetScope imagery paired with Sentinel-2-derived field boundary polygons is introduced, showing that higher-resolution imagery significantly improves field delineation performance, especially for small parcels.
AI.motivation: Smallholder parcels are only a few Sentinel-2 pixels wide, making accurate field boundary mapping challenging at 10 m resolution. The authors aim to evaluate whether 3 m imagery substantially improves field delineation quality for these small fields.
AI.method: FTP provides 133,168 co-registered PlanetScope patch-window targets across 24 countries, using the same polygons, seasonal windows, and train/test splits as the existing FTW dataset. Evaluation uses panoptic quality (PQ), object F1, size-stratified PQ, and meter-scale matched-boundary error, with vectorization of predictions before scoring.
AI.result: Under matched architectures and training recipes, 3 m imagery raises PQ from 21.0 to 35.5, PQ on sub-0.5 ha fields from 5.8 to 15.7, and cuts matched-boundary error from 18.6 m to 7.4 m.
AI.conclusion: The 3 m PlanetScope imagery yields substantially better field delineation than 10 m Sentinel-2, particularly for very small fields, reducing boundary errors by more than half.

title: FUSE: FK-Steered Multi-Modal Flow Matching for Efficient Simulation-Based Posterior Estimation
comment: Accepted to the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2026). 22 pages, 5 figures
summary: Simulation-Based Inference (SBI) is critical for scientific discovery, with generative models offering a promising path toward efficient inference. However, existing methods struggle with effective multimodal modeling. They often rely on brute-force fusion strategies that ignore the structural disparities between parameters and observations, thus limiting estimation fidelity. In this work, we introduce FUSE (Feynman-Kac steered mUlti-modal flow matching for efficient Simulation-based posterior Estimation). Unlike prior work, FUSE employs a dual-track architecture that preserves the distinct features of multimodal inputs while facilitating dynamic interaction. Additionally, we propose an FK-steered sampling strategy that leverages intermediate observation likelihoods to guide the generative trajectories, effectively improving the sample quality during inference. Our approach outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on standard SBI benchmarks, producing posteriors that closely match ground-truth MCMC. Furthermore, in a real-world exoplanet orbital estimation task, FUSE successfully resolves complex parameter degeneracies that challenge existing methods, highlighting its potential to accelerate complex scientific discoveries in astrophysics and beyond.

AI.tldr: FUSE introduces a dual-track architecture with Feynman-Kac steered flow matching for efficient multimodal simulation-based inference, outperforming baselines on SBI benchmarks and real-world exoplanet orbital estimation.
AI.motivation: Existing SBI methods struggle with effective multimodal modeling, relying on brute-force fusion that ignores structural disparities between parameters and observations, limiting estimation fidelity.
AI.method: FUSE employs (1) a dual-track architecture preserving distinct multimodal features while enabling dynamic interaction, and (2) an FK-steered sampling strategy using intermediate observation likelihoods to guide generative trajectories.
AI.result: Outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on standard SBI benchmarks, producing posteriors closely matching ground-truth MCMC. In exoplanet orbital estimation, successfully resolves complex parameter degeneracies.
AI.conclusion: FUSE demonstrates potential to accelerate complex scientific discoveries in astrophysics and beyond through improved multimodal simulation-based posterior estimation.

title: CCFM: Collision-Constrained Flow Matching for Safety-Critical Scenario Generation
summary: Evaluation of autonomous vehicle (AV) planners in safety-critical closed-loop simulation is essential for real-world deployment. However, generating controllable safety-critical scenarios remains challenging. Existing approaches use soft guidance that provides only probabilistic preferences and cannot guarantee the satisfaction of geometric and severity constraints associated with specific collision types. We introduce Collision-Constrained Flow Matching (CCFM), a novel framework that guarantees precise collision control through hard physical constraints. CCFM consists of three key components: (i) a heuristic collision selector that optimally identifies an adversarial agent and collision type via composite scoring; (ii) structured hard constraints that explicitly define four collision types (rear-end, side, cut-in, head-on) through contact point, heading, and severity requirements; and (iii) a collision-constrained flow matching sampler that enforces the constraints via Gauss-Newton manifold projection. CCFM achieves collision rate up to 46.4% on nuScenes and 83.1% on nuPlan, significantly outperforming baselines while preserving realistic driving behavior. By enabling controllable collision characteristics in safety-critical scenario generation, CCFM provides a reliable foundation for AV safety evaluation and sim-to-real crash data generation. The code and implementation details are available at https://github.com/KELISBU/CCFM.

AI.tldr: CCFM is a novel framework that uses collision-constrained flow matching with hard physical constraints to generate controllable safety-critical scenarios for autonomous vehicle testing, achieving collision rates of 46.4% on nuScenes and 83.1% on nuPlan.
AI.motivation: Existing approaches for generating safety-critical scenarios for AV evaluation rely on soft guidance that provides only probabilistic preferences and cannot guarantee satisfaction of geometric and severity constraints associated with specific collision types.
AI.method: CCFM consists of three components: (1) a heuristic collision selector for optimal adversarial agent and collision type identification via composite scoring; (2) structured hard constraints defining four collision types (rear-end, side, cut-in, head-on) via contact point, heading, and severity requirements; (3) a collision-constrained flow matching sampler enforcing constraints via Gauss-Newton manifold projection.
AI.result: CCFM achieves collision rates of 46.4% on nuScenes and 83.1% on nuPlan, significantly outperforming baselines while preserving realistic driving behavior.
AI.conclusion: CCFM enables controllable collision characteristics in safety-critical scenario generation, providing a reliable foundation for AV safety evaluation and sim-to-real crash data generation.

title: GeoFlow: Geo-Aware Modeling of Inter-Area Relationships in Origin-Destination Flow Prediction and Generation
summary: Origin-destination (OD) flow modeling underpins urban planning and mobility analysis, but prevailing graph-based methods often neglect salient geographic attributes, limiting their ability to model long-range and multi-area dependencies. In this paper, we introduce GeoFlow, a novel framework that (i) augments area representations with geospatial attributes, including relative positions, k-hop and geodesic distances, (ii) employs a specialized geometric-intrinsic fusion encoder design that combines graph attention for intrinsic area signals with coordinate-aware encoders for global structure, and (iii) adopts an axial-global attention decoder to capture OD-specific competitive dependencies. For OD flow generation, GeoFlow is paired with flow matching models to produce more authentic and diverse mobility samples. Empirically, GeoFlow achieves superior performance in predictive accuracy, while substantially improving generative fidelity and diversity. Ablation and analytical studies confirm the contribution of each component. Code is available at https://github.com/ZheruiHuang/GeoFlow.

AI.tldr: GeoFlow is a framework that enhances OD flow modeling by integrating geospatial attributes, geometric-intrinsic fusion encoder, and axial-global attention decoder with flow matching models for superior predictive accuracy and generative quality.
AI.motivation: Existing graph-based OD flow methods neglect salient geographic attributes, limiting their ability to model long-range and multi-area dependencies.
AI.method: GeoFlow (i) augments area representations with geospatial attributes (relative positions, k-hop/geodesic distances), (ii) uses a geometric-intrinsic fusion encoder combining graph attention for intrinsic signals with coordinate-aware encoders for global structure, and (iii) adopts an axial-global attention decoder for OD-specific competitive dependencies, paired with flow matching models for generation.
AI.result: GeoFlow achieves superior predictive accuracy and substantially improves generative fidelity and diversity; ablation studies confirm each component's contribution.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating geospatial attributes and specialized encoder-decoder design with flow matching significantly enhances OD flow modeling performance.

title: Spatial Graph Representation and Morphometric Analysis of the Pulmonary Vascular Tree From Computed Tomography Using Multi-Scale Hessian-Based Filter Fusion and TEASAR Skeletonization
summary: Reconstructing the pulmonary vascular tree from computed tomography (CT) images is essential for quantitative lung analysis, vascular morphology assessment, and patient-specific modeling, yet it remains challenging because vessels span multiple scales, from proximal arteries to distal microvasculature. Clinical chest CT is further affected by limited spatial resolution, partial volume effects, heterogeneous image quality, and respiratory motion artifacts. Unlike deep learning-based pulmonary vessel segmentation methods that require large annotated datasets, we propose a deterministic, training-free, and explainable pipeline for CT-based pulmonary vascular tree reconstruction. The method fuses multiscale Hessian-based Frangi and Sato vesselness filters using a weighted maximum response across 12 spatial scales from 1 to 8 mm, enabling detection of large pulmonary arteries and peripheral branches. Lung parenchyma is segmented by Hounsfield unit thresholding, morphological post-processing, and Chan-Vese active contour refinement. Vascular centerlines are extracted using the Kimimaro implementation of the TEASAR algorithm; separate left- and right-lung vascular graphs are then constructed, pruned, and verified for acyclicity. Geometric plausibility is assessed using volumetric fractal dimension, Strahler order analysis, Horton ratios, and Murray's law. The resulting fractal dimension of approximately 2.3 is consistent with reported values for the human pulmonary vasculature. At the same time, residual deviations in branching metrics reflect distal-vessel truncation caused by finite CT resolution. These results indicate that the proposed explainable pipeline can generate geometrically plausible pulmonary vascular tree models and may support quantitative pulmonary imaging, vascular morphometry, and computational lung modeling.

AI.tldr: A deterministic, training-free pipeline reconstructs pulmonary vascular trees from CT images using multiscale Hessian-based vesselness filters, Kimimaro/TEASAR centerline extraction, and geometric validation via fractal dimension (~2.3) and branching metrics.
AI.motivation: Pulmonary vascular tree reconstruction from CT is clinically important but challenging due to multiscale vessel structures, limited spatial resolution, partial volume effects, heterogeneous image quality, and motion artifacts. Existing deep learning methods require large annotated datasets.
AI.method: Multiscale Hessian-based Frangi and Sato vesselness filters (12 scales, 1–8 mm) with weighted maximum response fusion; HU thresholding + morphological processing + Chan-Vese active contour for lung segmentation; Kimimaro (TEASAR) for centerline extraction; left/right vascular graph construction, pruning, and acyclicity verification; geometric validation using fractal dimension, Strahler order, Horton ratios, and Murray's law.
AI.result: Fractal dimension ~2.3, consistent with reported human pulmonary vasculature values. Residual deviations in branching metrics reflect distal-vessel truncation due to finite CT resolution.
AI.conclusion: The explainable, training-free pipeline generates geometrically plausible pulmonary vascular tree models and may support quantitative pulmonary imaging, vascular morphometry, and computational lung modeling.

title: Target-Guided Selective Reweighting for Physics-Informed Neural Network Inverse Problems: A Transfer Learning Approach
summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) encounter ill-posed optimization, loss competition, and parameter compensation in partial differential equation (PDE) inverse problems. Transfer learning can reuse representations from source tasks, but direct fine-tuning may introduce negative transfer when dominant physical mechanisms, governing parameters, or observation noise differ between source and target domains: the model achieves low field error yet recovers incorrect target physical parameters. To mitigate, we propose Target-Guided Selective Reweighting PINN (TGSR-PINN), a target-evidence-driven representation correction method for PINN inverse transfer learning. TGSR-PINN transfers only the weights and biases from the source PINN, while target physical parameters are independently initialized; after a short target-adaptation phase, the method computes neuron target scores using first-order Taylor sensitivity and pre-activation variance on fixed scoring batches, and converts evidence associated with low-scoring neurons into continuous weak-adaptation signals via a Gaussian mixture model (GMM) with rank fallback. TGSR-PINN then applies selective soft decay to input weight rows and biases of low-scoring neurons instead of hard pruning or random resetting. In experiments, TGSR-PINN improves target parameter recovery while maintaining comparable field accuracy in the high-Péclet 2D advection-diffusion task and in the Allen--Cahn to Burgers cross-PDE-family transfer task; a 5%-noise reaction--diffusion case provides supplementary evidence under milder source-target mismatch. Ablation studies suggest that neuron target scoring, weak-adaptation signal estimation, layer protection, and selective soft decay jointly contribute to the benefits.

AI.tldr: TGSR-PINN mitigates negative transfer in PINN inverse problems by selectively soft-decaying low-scoring neurons based on target-evidence-driven scoring, improving target parameter recovery without sacrificing field accuracy.
AI.motivation: PINNs suffer from ill-posed optimization and negative transfer in inverse PDE problems when source-target domain discrepancies exist (e.g., differing governing parameters, noise levels), causing correct field error but incorrect parameter recovery.
AI.method: TGSR-PINN transfers only source weights/biases; independently initializes target parameters; computes neuron target scores via first-order Taylor sensitivity & pre-activation variance; applies GMM with rank fallback to identify low-scoring neurons; selectively soft-decays their input weights and biases instead of hard pruning or resetting.
AI.result: Improves target parameter recovery with comparable field accuracy in high-Péclet 2D advection-diffusion and Allen-Cahn to Burgers cross-PDE-family tasks; supplementary 5%-noise reaction-diffusion evidence. Ablation confirms joint benefit of scoring, weak-adaptation estimation, layer protection, and soft decay.
AI.conclusion: Target-evidence-driven selective reweighting is effective for PINN inverse transfer learning under source-target mismatch.

title: Flash-BoN: Instant Drafts for Inference-Time Scaling in Diffusion Models
summary: Inference-time scaling for text-to-image generation has progressed from simple Best-of-$N$ (BoN) sampling to guided search methods that verify and steer candidate trajectories at intermediate denoising steps. These approaches focus on when and how often to verify during denoising but largely treat the cost of generation itself as fixed. Moreover, the standard practice of comparing methods by number of function evaluations (NFEs) counts only denoising forward passes and ignores verifier overhead, which can distort efficiency rankings. We show that under wall-clock evaluation, simple BoN already matches or outperforms several guided search techniques, suggesting that compute is better spent on broader exploration than on repeated intermediate verification. This motivates Flash-BoN, which generates a large pool of inexpensive draft candidates by combining three complementary acceleration knobs: timestep truncation, layer skipping, and activation proxies into a single configuration optimized once per model. An efficient multi-stage verification procedure then identifies the most promising draft, which is refined at full quality. Across three benchmarks and three model scales, Flash-BoN consistently outperforms all baselines under fixed wall-clock budgets, with gains that grow at larger model scales (+8% AUC). We further show that our strategy combines well and improves existing orthogonal techniques such as reflection-based prompt optimization (+16% AUC). The gains correlate with increased candidate diversity, which also enables draft-guided selection to accelerate RL post-training convergence.

AI.tldr: Flash-BoN improves text-to-image generation by efficiently combining timestep truncation, layer skipping, and activation proxies to produce cheap draft candidates, then verifying and refining them, outperforming existing methods under wall-clock evaluation.
AI.motivation: Current inference-time scaling methods for text-to-image generation focus on when/how often to verify during denoising but treat generation cost as fixed. Standard NFE-based evaluation ignores verifier overhead, distorting efficiency rankings. Under wall-clock measurement, simple BoN already matches or outperforms guided search, suggesting compute is better spent on broader exploration.
AI.method: Flash-BoN generates a large pool of inexpensive draft candidates using three acceleration knobs (timestep truncation, layer skipping, activation proxies) configured per model, applies efficient multi-stage verification to select the best draft, then refines it at full quality.
AI.result: Flash-BoN consistently outperforms all baselines under fixed wall-clock budgets across three benchmarks and three model scales, with gains growing at larger scales (+8% AUC). It also improves reflection-based prompt optimization (+16% AUC) and accelerates RL post-training convergence via draft-guided selection.
AI.conclusion: Broader exploration via cheap drafting is more effective than repeated intermediate verification for inference-time scaling in text-to-image generation. Flash-BoN's gains correlate with increased candidate diversity.

title: Adaptive Inference Batching using Policy Gradients
summary:
Inference serving systems must balance throughput and latency under bursty, heterogeneous workloads, yet the industry standard remains static batching policies that require manual tuning and cannot adapt to shifting traffic. We investigate whether reinforcement learning (RL) can learn adaptive batching and routing policies that outperform these heuristics, training REINFORCE and PPO agents on a discrete-event simulator validated against queuing theory and production traces (Azure Functions, BurstGPT). We formulate the problem as an MDP over queue state, request type and GPU availability, evaluating across standard Poisson traffic, extreme bursts, real-world traces and heterogeneous multi-GPU routing.
  Our central finding is a clear boundary condition for RL's value in systems problems. In single-GPU settings, a well-tuned static batching policy is already near-optimal under Poisson-like arrivals and RL offers only marginal gains (+0.1% to +1.0%). In multi-GPU heterogeneous routing, however, where fast and slow requests compete for shared resources, the agent discovers a workload-segregation policy that eliminates Head-of-Line blocking, yielding a 3.5x (348%) improvement over Round-Robin and a 48% improvement over the strongest heuristic baseline (Shortest-Queue), with 60% higher throughput and 25% lower latency while respecting SLA constraints. The policy generalizes to unseen bursty and real-world traffic despite training only on synthetic Poisson arrivals and an attention-augmented policy network converges roughly 20% faster than an MLP baseline.
  These results suggest RL's advantage over engineered heuristics concentrates in combinatorial, multi-resource decisions rather than single-resource temporal scheduling, a practical distinction for deciding where learned policies justify their engineering cost in production inference infrastructure.

AI.tldr: RL-based adaptive batching and routing policies outperform static heuristics in multi-GPU heterogeneous inference serving (3.5x improvement over Round-Robin) but offer only marginal gains (+0.1–1.0%) in single-GPU settings, revealing a clear boundary condition where RL's value concentrates in combinatorial multi-resource decisions.
AI.motivation: Inference serving systems rely on static batching policies that require manual tuning and cannot adapt to bursty, heterogeneous workloads; the paper investigates whether RL can learn adaptive policies that outperform these heuristics.
AI.method: Formulates batching and routing as an MDP over queue state, request type, and GPU availability; trains REINFORCE and PPO agents on a discrete-event simulator validated against queuing theory and production traces (Azure Functions, BurstGPT); evaluates across Poisson traffic, extreme bursts, real-world traces, and heterogeneous multi-GPU routing with attention-augmented policy networks.
AI.result: Single-GPU: static batching near-optimal (RL gains +0.1% to +1.0%). Multi-GPU heterogeneous routing: RL discovers workload-segregation policy eliminating Head-of-Line blocking, achieving 3.5x (348%) improvement over Round-Robin, 48% improvement over Shortest-Queue, 60% higher throughput, 25% lower latency under SLA constraints. Attention-augmented policy converges ~20% faster than MLP baseline.
AI.conclusion: RL's advantage over engineered heuristics concentrates in combinatorial, multi-resource decisions rather than single-resource temporal scheduling, providing a practical guideline for deciding where learned policies justify their engineering cost in production inference infrastructure.

title: EVAS: Efficient Multimodal Temporal Forgery Localization via Audio-Visual Synergy and Steered Boundary Calibration
summary: The rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence-generated content necessitates reliable multimodal forensics. Beyond video-level binary classification, precisely localizing sparsely distributed forged segments in long-form videos remains a critical challenge. This task is particularly difficult when manipulations are subtly embedded and cross-modal signals are weak and temporally diffuse. To address these challenges, we propose EVAS, an end-to-end multimodal framework for temporal forgery localization. At its core, a Multi-Stage Audio-Visual Synergy mechanism facilitates progressive cross-modal interaction to learn deep multimodal forensic representations and capture high-order semantic traces of sparse manipulations. Furthermore, we introduce a Boundary-Aware Refinement strategy to achieve steered boundary calibration. By incorporating invalid-frame masking, this strategy suppresses ambiguous regions and sharpens transition predictions. We adopt a decoupled training paradigm with auxiliary heads to disentangle representation learning from inference objectives, enhancing model generalization and stability. Additionally, a lightweight HourglassFFN is incorporated to reduce computational overhead. Extensive experiments demonstrate that EVAS achieves state-of-the-art average localization accuracy and average recall across three benchmark datasets, validating its effectiveness for fine-grained temporal forgery localization.

AI.tldr: EVAS is an end-to-end multimodal framework for temporal forgery localization in long-form videos, using Multi-Stage Audio-Visual Synergy, Boundary-Aware Refinement, decoupled training, and HourglassFFN to achieve state-of-the-art performance on three benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing methods struggle with precisely localizing sparsely distributed forged segments in long-form videos, especially when manipulations are subtly embedded and cross-modal signals are weak and temporally diffuse. Beyond video-level binary classification, fine-grained temporal forgery localization remains a critical challenge.
AI.method: EVAS employs: (1) a Multi-Stage Audio-Visual Synergy mechanism for progressive cross-modal interaction to learn deep multimodal forensic representations; (2) a Boundary-Aware Refinement strategy with invalid-frame masking for steered boundary calibration; (3) a decoupled training paradigm with auxiliary heads to disentangle representation learning from inference; and (4) a lightweight HourglassFFN to reduce computational overhead.
AI.result: EVAS achieves state-of-the-art average localization accuracy and average recall across three benchmark datasets for fine-grained temporal forgery localization.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework effectively addresses the challenges of subtle, sparse manipulation localization in long-form videos, and its design components (multi-stage synergy, boundary refinement, decoupled training) collectively contribute to superior performance and generalization.

title: Advances in Neural Controlled Differential Equations
comment: DPhil thesis, University of Oxford, 188 pages, 17 figures
summary:
Many real-world systems evolve continuously, yet most machine learning models interpret time series as discrete sequences. Continuous-time approaches instead treat time series as samples from an underlying input path, a formulation that naturally accommodates irregularly sampled or oversampled data. Among these, Neural Controlled Differential Equations (NCDEs) are a maximally expressive class of models that parametrise a vector field using a neural network and evolve their hidden state by solving a dynamical system driven by the input path. NCDEs typically use a non-linear vector field, so their expressive power and continuous-time flexibility come at the cost of a forward pass that is both computationally expensive and inherently sequential, limiting their scalability and practical applicability.
  This thesis advances the training and scalability of NCDEs through three complementary contributions. First, building on neural rough differential equations, Log-NCDEs apply the Log-ODE method to efficiently approximate an NCDE's solution during training, improving both computational speed and empirical performance. Second, Linear NCDEs replace the non-linear vector field with a linear one, enabling closed-form solutions and parallel-in-time computation without sacrificing theoretical expressivity. Third, Structured Linear NCDEs use structured linear vector fields to further enhance efficiency while maintaining theoretical expressiveness and empirical performance.
  Collectively, these methods reduce the time per training step for an NCDE by up to three orders of magnitude while achieving state-of-the-art performance across diverse time series benchmarks.

AI.tldr: This thesis improves the training efficiency and scalability of Neural Controlled Differential Equations (NCDEs) for continuous-time time series modeling through three contributions: Log-NCDEs (using Log-ODE method for faster approximation), Linear NCDEs (closed-form solutions via linear vector fields), and Structured Linear NCDEs (structured linear fields for further efficiency), collectively reducing training time per step by up to 1000x while maintaining state-of-the-art performance.
AI.motivation: NCDEs are expressive continuous-time models for irregularly sampled time series, but their non-linear vector field makes the forward pass computationally expensive and inherently sequential, limiting scalability and practical applicability.
AI.method: Three methods: (1) Log-NCDEs apply the Log-ODE method for efficient approximation during training; (2) Linear NCDEs replace non-linear vector fields with linear ones enabling closed-form parallel-in-time solutions; (3) Structured Linear NCDEs use structured linear vector fields for additional efficiency gains.
AI.result: Reduces time per training step for NCDEs by up to three orders of magnitude (1000x) while achieving state-of-the-art performance across diverse time series benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: NCDEs can be made significantly more computationally efficient and scalable through approximation techniques (Log-ODE) and architectural simplifications (linear/structured linear vector fields) without sacrificing expressive power or empirical performance.

title: PulmoSight-XAI: An Explainable Multi-View Attention Ensemble with Gradient Boosting Meta-Learning for Multi-Label Chest X-Ray Classification
summary: Automated chest X-ray classification remains challenging due to severe class imbalance, co-occurring pathologies, and the loss of localized features in conventional architectures. To address these, we propose an explainable hierarchical multi-view ensemble framework for the robust classification of 14 thoracic pathologies. The framework employs view-specific training by independently modeling frontal and lateral radiographs using an ensemble of five complementary convolutional neural networks. Replacing global average pooling, a multi-scale feature fusion strategy augmented with Convolutional Block Attention Modules (CBAM) preserves fine-grained intermediate representations while emphasizing high-level pathology-specific semantic features. To mitigate positive-negative imbalance and varying inter-class difficulty, models are optimized using a novel hybrid objective combining Asymmetric Loss with Adaptive Focal Loss. Beyond simple probability averaging, the framework incorporates a hierarchical meta-learning strategy where test-time augmentation (TTA) predictions and cross-model uncertainty measures are integrated into Level-1 gradient-boosting meta-learners (XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost), followed by Level-2 stacking with optimized alpha blending. Evaluated on a large-scale CheXpert-style dataset, the framework achieves state-of-the-art macro-average AUROC scores of 0.9319 for frontal and 0.9154 for lateral radiographs. Furthermore, comprehensive explainability analysis using seven post-hoc attribution techniques demonstrates strong anatomical consistency and clinically meaningful decision localization. By integrating architectural diversity, multi-scale attention, hierarchical meta-learning, and rigorous explainability, the proposed framework provides a transparent, highly accurate, and clinically practical computer-aided diagnosis system for thoracic disease classification.

AI.tldr: A hierarchical multi-view ensemble framework using view-specific CNNs, multi-scale attention (CBAM), a hybrid Asymmetric + Adaptive Focal loss, and two-level meta-learning (XGBoost/LightGBM/CatBoost + stacking) achieves state-of-the-art chest X-ray classification (macro AUROC 0.9319 frontal, 0.9154 lateral) with comprehensive explainability on 14 thoracic pathologies.
AI.motivation: To overcome severe class imbalance, co-occurring pathologies, and localized feature loss in conventional CNN architectures for automated chest X-ray classification.
AI.method: (1) View-specific training with an ensemble of five CNNs on frontal/lateral radiographs. (2) Multi-scale feature fusion + CBAM replacing global average pooling. (3) Hybrid loss: Asymmetric Loss + Adaptive Focal Loss. (4) Hierarchical meta-learning: Level-1 (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) on TTA predictions and uncertainty measures; Level-2 stacking with optimized alpha blending.
AI.result: State-of-the-art macro-average AUROC of 0.9319 (frontal) and 0.9154 (lateral) on a large-scale CheXpert-style dataset; strong anatomical consistency in explainability analysis using seven post-hoc attribution techniques.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework offers a transparent, highly accurate, and clinically practical CAD system for thoracic disease classification by integrating architectural diversity, multi-scale attention, hierarchical meta-learning, and rigorous explainability.

title: Air Quality Downscaling with Station-Guided Pseudo-Supervision
summary: Super-resolving coarse atmospheric fields to local PM$_{2.5}$ variations is uniquely challenged by a mismatch in spatial support: while pixels represent regional averages, ground-truth observations are discrete, unaligned samples of a continuous spatial signal. To bridge this gap, we present a station-guided framework for high-resolution PM$_{2.5}$ downscaling over Europe. Taking coarse CAMS atmospheric composition fields alongside heterogeneous side information (i.e., human activity, land cover, elevation, satellite aerosol observations, and wind fields) our framework jointly super-resolves ($\times 40$, $\approx$ 1 km) and bias-corrects CAMS rasters, without relying on temporal sequence modelling. To address the challenge of densely supervising our multi-scale transformer network with sparse in-situ data, we introduce a time-agnostic propagation strategy that utilises spatial Gaussian blending of interpolated OpenAQ observations. Extensive qualitative and station-level evaluations across Europe demonstrate that our model recovers fine-grained spatial structures and effectively mitigates localised CAMS biases.

AI.tldr: A station-guided framework using multi-scale transformers and time-agnostic Gaussian propagation to super-resolve CAMS PM2.5 fields from coarse (~40km) to ~1km resolution while correcting biases, validated across Europe.
AI.motivation: The mismatch between coarse atmospheric raster pixels (regional averages) and discrete ground-truth PM2.5 observations (unaligned samples) makes super-resolution uniquely challenging; existing methods lack a framework to bridge this spatial support gap.
AI.method: A multi-scale transformer network jointly super-resolves (×40, ~1km) and bias-corrects CAMS fields using heterogeneous side information (human activity, land cover, elevation, satellite AOD, wind). A time-agnostic propagation strategy with spatial Gaussian blending of interpolated OpenAQ observations addresses sparse in-situ supervision.
AI.result: The model recovers fine-grained spatial structures and effectively mitigates localized CAMS biases in qualitative and station-level evaluations across Europe.
AI.conclusion: The proposed station-guided framework successfully bridges the spatial support gap for PM2.5 downscaling without temporal sequencing, producing high-resolution bias-corrected estimates.

title: TrustCLIP: Learning Private Visual Features via Adversarial Reconstruction
summary: Vision and vision-language models rely on high-level visual representations that are increasingly used across recognition, retrieval, and multimodal reasoning pipelines. However, recent advances in generative modeling have shown that such features can often be inverted, enabling realistic reconstructions of the underlying image and raising significant privacy risks. We revisit this problem through the lens of reconstruction and propose TrustCLIP, a reconstruction-driven framework that treats a feature-conditioned generator as an explicit privacy adversary. TrustCLIP learns a projection between encoder features and downstream modules that is explicitly optimized to degrade the reconstructions produced by generative attackers while retaining the necessary signals for downstream tasks. Unlike prior defenses that rely on discriminative privacy metrics, TrustCLIP directly optimizes against a generative reconstruction attacker, targeting a threat not captured by standard evaluation protocols. We demonstrate its effectiveness in both conventional classification and multimodal large language model pipelines. Across these settings, TrustCLIP consistently reduces the fidelity of generative inversions while maintaining downstream task performance. Project page: https://atnikos.github.io/trustclip/

AI.tldr: TrustCLIP is a reconstruction-driven framework that protects privacy by learning a projection that degrades generative inversions of visual features while preserving downstream task performance.
AI.motivation: High-level visual representations from vision and vision-language models can be inverted by generative models to reconstruct realistic images, posing significant privacy risks that are not adequately addressed by existing discriminative privacy metrics.
AI.method: TrustCLIP learns a projection between encoder features and downstream modules that is explicitly optimized to degrade reconstructions produced by generative attackers while retaining necessary signals for downstream tasks.
AI.result: TrustCLIP consistently reduces the fidelity of generative inversions while maintaining downstream task performance in both conventional classification and multimodal large language model pipelines.
AI.conclusion: Directly optimizing against generative reconstruction attackers provides a more effective privacy defense than discriminative privacy metrics, addressing a threat not captured by standard evaluation protocols.

title: Learning Only What Valid Adapters Can Express: Subspace-Constrained Adaptation Against Fine-Tuning Poisoning
comment: 10 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/infinition/z-manifold
summary: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning still leaves a broad space of behavior-changing updates reachable, so a poisoned objective can be represented and optimized. We study an alternative: adaptation constrained to the subspace estimated from a trusted pool of existing task adapters. On flan-t5-large with 196 public LoRA adapters, we show that (1) the functionally relevant content of an adapter lies in a low-dimensional shared subspace, 30 to 38 percent of its weight norm being redundant under the evaluated task distributions; (2) gradient adaptation restricted to 128 coordinates on this subspace matches full LoRA fine-tuning on clean classification data, while under targeted label inversion LoRA collapses to 3-26 percent exact match and the constrained learner keeps 62-96 percent on the tasks the pool covers; (3) the constrained learner cannot fit corrupted data, its adaptation loss separating clean from garbage by two orders of magnitude (120x), an out-of-distribution signal without an extra detector; and (4) against an adaptive backdoor attacker who optimizes within the subspace, the attack is blocked (8 percent success versus 100 for LoRA) on the task where its target behavior is unlike anything in the pool, and only partially blocked (85 percent) when the target coincides with a common pool behavior. On these two tasks the outcome is consistent with how close the target is to the pool's directions, which suggests but does not establish a pool-relative boundary. The mechanism trades peak plasticity for these properties: on tasks the pool covers poorly, unconstrained fine-tuning wins, and the protection assumes the pool itself is trusted. Code and data are public.

AI.tldr: Constraining fine-tuning to a subspace estimated from a trusted pool of existing adapters (e.g., 196 public LoRA adapters on flan-t5-large) prevents poisoned updates and backdoor attacks while maintaining performance on covered tasks, at the cost of plasticity on tasks the pool covers poorly.
AI.motivation: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) remains vulnerable to poisoned objectives that can be represented and optimized in the broad space of behavior-changing updates. The authors study a constrained adaptation method to mitigate this security risk.
AI.method: The method restricts adaptation to a low-dimensional subspace estimated from a trusted pool of existing task adapters. On flan-t5-large with 196 public LoRA adapters, the authors analyze the functional subspace, constrain gradient updates to 128 coordinates, and evaluate against clean data, label inversion, and adaptive backdoor attacks.
AI.result: (1) 30-38% of adapter weight norm is redundant; (2) constrained learner matches full LoRA on clean data but resists label inversion (62-96% vs 3-26%); (3) loss separates clean from corrupted data by 120x; (4) adaptive backdoor attack blocked (8% vs 100% success) when target behavior is unlike pool, partially blocked (85%) when target coincides with common pool behavior.
AI.conclusion: Subspace-constrained adaptation provides strong protection against poisoning and backdoor attacks on tasks covered by the trusted pool, but trades peak plasticity for these safety properties. Protection assumes the pool itself is trustworthy.

title: Enhancing Facial Expression Recognition in Head-Mounted Displays with Synthetic Data
summary: Facial expression recognition (FER) is crucial for social interaction in mixed reality environments that employ head-mounted displays (HMD). However, collecting FER data from head-mounted cameras (HMC) is challenging due to privacy concerns and the diversity of HMD platforms. Moreover, existing FER datasets are not directly applicable due to the unique perspectives of HMCs. The lack of sufficient data hinders the development of neural network-based HMC FER methods. To address data scarcity, we propose a data synthesis framework that generates HMC-view images from frontal-view images, leveraging abundant existing annotated datasets. Specifically, we first reconstruct 3D textured meshes from images and then apply a configurable camera system to render images from the HMC perspective. Additionally, we introduce a texture-space alignment network (TSAN) that enables accurate texture sampling from images to preserve detailed facial expressions. To evaluate the proposed method, we conduct extensive experiments on both simulated and real HMC datasets.
