ProCon softly projects each test patch onto nearby normal memory vectors and uses the projection residual as anomaly evidence. To stabilize this residual, it constructs seed-perturbed layer-wise memories, aggregates bank residuals by a median, and fuses depth-specific residual maps by layer consensus. ProCon requires no decoder training, backbone fine-tuning, learned fusion weights, or pseudo-anomaly supervision. Across MVTec-AD, VisA, and Real-IAD under the single-category evaluation protocol, ProCon achieves strong image- and pixel-level performance under seven standard metrics, including image AUROC scores of 99.8%, 99.2%, and 93.2%, respectively. Ablations show that the gains come from replacing hard retrieval with soft normal projection and stabilizing the residuals through memory and depth consensus. The code is available at https://github.com/jw-chae/Procon

AI.tldr: ProCon is a training-free, memory-based anomaly detection framework that replaces hard nearest-neighbor retrieval with soft normal projection and stabilizes residuals via seed-perturbed memories, median aggregation, and layer consensus, achieving state-of-the-art results on MVTec-AD (99.8% AUROC), VisA (99.2%), and Real-IAD (93.2%).
AI.motivation: Existing memory-based anomaly detection methods treat memory as a nearest-neighbor lookup table (hard retrieval), which is vulnerable to false-normal matches and fails to verify whether a test patch is consistently supported by a local normal neighborhood.
AI.method: ProCon softly projects each test patch onto nearby normal memory vectors, uses the projection residual as anomaly evidence, constructs seed-perturbed layer-wise memories, aggregates bank residuals by median, and fuses depth-specific residual maps via layer consensus—all without decoder training, backbone fine-tuning, learned fusion weights, or pseudo-anomaly supervision.
AI.result: On MVTec-AD, VisA, and Real-IAD under single-category evaluation, ProCon achieves image AUROC scores of 99.8%, 99.2%, and 93.2% respectively, with strong performance across seven standard metrics at both image and pixel levels.
AI.conclusion: Replacing hard retrieval with soft normal projection and stabilizing residuals through memory and depth consensus are the key contributors to ProCon's superior performance in anomaly detection.

title: 3DMPE: 3D Multi-Perspective Embedding
summary: We study 3D point cloud reconstruction from multiple partially observed 2D projections. Given two or more projections of an unknown 3D point cloud, together with cross-view point correspondences and visibility information, our goal is to recover a consistent 3D configuration when different views contain different subsets of points. We propose 3D Multi-Perspective Embedding (3DMPE), an optimization-based, training-free method that reconstructs the 3D point cloud and, in the variable-projection setting, jointly estimates the projection maps. 3DMPE extends Multi-Perspective Simultaneous Embedding to accommodate missing points and incomplete pairwise distance information across views. We consider both fixed-projection and variable-projection settings. Unlike learning-based reconstruction methods that infer shape from raw images and often depend on training data, 3DMPE operates on geometric observations with established correspondences and does not require category-specific training. Experiments on ShapeNet and Pix3D evaluate reconstruction quality using Chamfer Distance, Earth Mover Distance, and RMSE-Optimize-Align (ROA), and examine the effects of initialization, the number of views, point visibility, and several noise regimes, including noisy distances and erroneous correspondences. The results demonstrate that 3DMPE can effectively reconstruct point clouds from partial multi-view geometric observations.

AI.tldr: 3DMPE is an optimization-based, training-free method that reconstructs 3D point clouds from multiple partially observed 2D projections with cross-view correspondences, handling missing points and incomplete distance information across views.
AI.motivation: To reconstruct consistent 3D point clouds from multiple partial 2D projections when different views contain different subsets of points, without relying on training data or category-specific priors.
AI.method: 3DMPE extends Multi-Perspective Simultaneous Embedding to handle missing points and incomplete pairwise distance information across views, operating in both fixed-projection and variable-projection settings via optimization.
AI.result: Evaluated on ShapeNet and Pix3D using Chamfer Distance, Earth Mover Distance, and RMSE-Optimize-Align (ROA); robust across varying initialization, number of views, point visibility, and noise regimes including noisy distances and erroneous correspondences.
AI.conclusion: 3DMPE effectively reconstructs 3D point clouds from partial multi-view geometric observations without requiring training data or category-specific knowledge.

title: Graph Representation Learning of Longitudinal Medical Imaging Trajectories for Treatment Response Prediction
summary: In patients with breast cancer, pathological complete response (pCR) has been established as a clinically meaningful surrogate marker for long-term outcomes. While commonly treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT), effective treatment decision-making remains challenging, as therapeutic response can vary substantially across patients, calling for predictive models capable of accurately estimating individualized treatment response. To address this, we propose an imaging-based 3D spatio-temporal framework for treatment response prediction that integrates a state-of-the-art graph neural network with relational modeling of temporal interactions across timepoints alongside three novel complementary self-supervised treatment trajectory representation learning objectives. Experiments across a cohort of 585 patients from the public ISPY-2 dataset demonstrate that our method substantially outperforms both vision and self-supervised learning baselines across several classification metrics. Alongside establishing a breast cancer pCR prediction benchmark, we include a principled ablation of our method and further introduce and empirically assess the impact of the available number of DCE-MRI timepoints per patient trajectory and the inclusion of inter-scan time-differences. Overall, our study substantiates the utility of clinically meaningful longitudinal medical imagaging modeling for predicting NACT-induced pCR. We will publicly share our code repository and a user-friendly PyPI library for dataset curation upon publication, effectively promoting reproducible open-source research.

AI.tldr: A 3D spatio-temporal graph neural network with self-supervised learning objectives predicts pathological complete response (pCR) in breast cancer patients from longitudinal DCE-MRI, outperforming baselines on the ISPY-2 dataset (585 patients).
AI.motivation: Pathological complete response (pCR) is a surrogate marker for long-term outcomes in breast cancer, but treatment response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy varies greatly across patients. Accurate individualized prediction models are needed to support treatment decision-making.
AI.method: Proposed an imaging-based 3D spatio-temporal framework combining a graph neural network with relational modeling of temporal interactions across DCE-MRI timepoints, plus three complementary self-supervised treatment trajectory representation learning objectives.
AI.result: Outperforms vision and self-supervised learning baselines on multiple classification metrics using a cohort of 585 patients from the ISPY-2 dataset. Includes ablation studies, analysis of DCE-MRI timepoint count impact, and inter-scan time-difference effects.
AI.conclusion: Longitudinal medical imaging modeling is effective for predicting NACT-induced pCR in breast cancer. The study establishes a benchmark and will release code and a PyPI library to promote reproducible open-source research.

title: Efficient Perception in Automotive Detection and Tracking Using Neuromorphic Computing
summary: Deep learning algorithms are notorious for their high carbon footprint and computational demands that limit their deployment on edge devices and raise concerns about their long-term sustainability. Neuromorphic computing and Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer a promising alternative to traditional Von Neumann architectures, providing energy-efficient performance, massively parallel computation, and on-chip learning capabilities. Autonomous machines represent a critical application domain where these advantages are particularly valuable. We present the first comprehensive evaluation of SNNs for real-world automotive multi-object detection and tracking. Using transfer learning with the SpikeYOLO architecture, we achieve mean Average Precision of 0.937 on the KITTI dataset and 0.771 on BDD100K MOT2020 dataset for object detection and a Higher Order Tracking Accuracy score of 0.701 (KITTI) and 0.445 (BDD100K MOT2020) for object tracking--results competitive with conventional deep learning methods. Our results demonstrate that SNNs can deliver high-performance object detection and tracking in an energy efficient manner, establishing their viability for perception in real-world autonomous systems.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first comprehensive evaluation of Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) for real-world automotive multi-object detection and tracking. Using transfer learning with SpikeYOLO, the authors achieve competitive performance (0.937 mAP on KITTI, 0.771 on BDD100K for detection; 0.701 HOTA on KITTI, 0.445 on BDD100K for tracking) while maintaining energy efficiency, demonstrating SNNs as a viable alternative to conventional deep learning for autonomous systems.
AI.motivation: Deep learning algorithms suffer from high carbon footprint and computational demands that limit edge deployment and raise sustainability concerns. Neuromorphic computing and SNNs offer energy-efficient alternatives, but their viability for real-world autonomous perception tasks remained unverified.
AI.method: The authors perform the first comprehensive evaluation of SNNs for automotive multi-object detection and tracking using transfer learning with the SpikeYOLO architecture, tested on the KITTI and BDD100K MOT2020 datasets.
AI.result: Achieved 0.937 mAP (KITTI) and 0.771 mAP (BDD100K MOT2020) for detection; 0.701 HOTA (KITTI) and 0.445 HOTA (BDD100K) for tracking—competitive with conventional deep learning methods.
AI.conclusion: SNNs can deliver high-performance object detection and tracking in an energy-efficient manner, establishing their viability for perception in real-world autonomous systems.

title: UniSpine-GS: An Efficient Physics-Aware Gaussian Framework for Cross-Modality Multi-view Spine Image Synthesis
summary: The diagnosis of spinal diseases is often assisted by 3D imaging techniques in clinical practice. However, precise 3D spinal assessment is limited by the high costs of 3D imaging hardware and the challenges posed by the physical differences between imaging modalities, which hinder the generalizability of models. To address these issues, we propose UniSpine-GS, an efficient, physics-aware Gaussian framework designed for novel-view projection rendering in multi-view spine imaging via a 3D-aware representation. Instead of performing explicit 3D reconstruction, our approach learns a geometry-aware Gaussian representation that ensures anatomical consistency across different views. We introduce SPWM, a structure-guided loss reweighting strategy to improve boundary fidelity and local details. We evaluate our method on the CTSpine3D dataset and a newly constructed 3D fetal ultrasound dataset, FeSpine3D. Our results demonstrate that UniSpine-GS significantly outperforms existing methods across all metrics, offering a practical and cost-effective solution for unified multi-view medical imaging. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/orangeisland66/UniSpine-GS.

AI.tldr: UniSpine-GS is a physics-aware Gaussian framework for novel-view projection rendering in multi-view spine imaging, using a geometry-aware Gaussian representation with structure-guided loss reweighting (SPWM) to enable consistent, high-quality 3D spinal assessment without explicit 3D reconstruction. It outperforms existing methods on CTSpine3D and a new fetal ultrasound dataset (FeSpine3D).
AI.motivation: 3D spinal assessment is limited by high hardware costs of 3D imaging and poor cross-modality generalizability. Existing methods struggle with physical differences between imaging modalities, hindering practical deployment.
AI.method: UniSpine-GS learns a geometry-aware Gaussian representation for novel-view projection rendering without explicit 3D reconstruction. It introduces SPWM (Structure-guided loss reweighting) to improve boundary fidelity and local details.
AI.result: Evaluated on CTSpine3D and a newly constructed 3D fetal ultrasound dataset (FeSpine3D), UniSpine-GS significantly outperforms existing methods across all metrics.
AI.conclusion: UniSpine-GS offers a practical, cost-effective solution for unified multi-view medical imaging, with publicly available code.

title: MemPose: Category-level Object Pose Estimation with Memory
summary: In the pursuit of robust and generalizable category-level object pose estimation, most existing methods adopt parametric formulations that learn effective representations from data, yet they primarily encode category-level patterns into fixed shape priors or static parameter weights, which limits their scalability to highly diverse instances. In this paper, we rethink category-level pose estimation from a memory-centric perspective and present MemPose, a memory-augmented framework that explicitly incorporates category-level geometric memory into the pose estimation pipeline. We introduce an external memory buffer that stores and dynamically updates structural representations from previously observed instances, enabling the model to leverage accumulated experience to support current perception. Extensive experiments on four challenging benchmarks (REAL275, CAMERA25, Housecat6D and Wild6D) demonstrate the superiority of our proposed method over previous state-of-the-art approaches.

AI.tldr: MemPose introduces a memory-augmented framework for category-level object pose estimation that stores and dynamically updates structural representations from previously observed instances, outperforming prior methods on four benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing category-level pose estimation methods use parametric formulations with fixed shape priors or static weights, limiting scalability to highly diverse instances. The authors aim to address this by rethinking pose estimation from a memory-centric perspective.
AI.method: MemPose incorporates an external memory buffer that stores and dynamically updates structural representations from previously observed instances, enabling the model to leverage accumulated experience to support current perception.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on four challenging benchmarks (REAL275, CAMERA25, Housecat6D, Wild6D) demonstrate superiority over previous state-of-the-art approaches.
AI.conclusion: The memory-augmented approach effectively addresses scalability limitations of parametric methods for category-level pose estimation, achieving robust and generalizable performance across diverse instances.

title: Virtual Category-Guided Continual Generalized Category Discovery
summary: Continual Generalized Category Discovery (C-GCD) aims to incrementally identify novel categories from sequential unlabeled data while preserving recognition of known classes, which is an essential capability for open-world visual learning. A major bottleneck lies in ambiguous unlabeled samples that cannot be confidently assigned to known classes nor reliably grouped as novel ones, making pseudo-labeling brittle and often biasing learning toward familiar categories. In this work, we introduce Virtual Category-Guided Continual Generalized Category Discovery by adapting Virtual Category Learning (VCL) to the continual setting. Our method identifies uncertain samples and assigns them to temporary virtual categories, enabling safe and informative learning from unlabeled streams without injecting noisy labels, while improving unlabeled data utilization and mitigating prediction bias. To further stabilize discovery across sessions and enhance class separation, we augment VCL with Expanded Neighborhood Contrastive Learning (ENCL), which exploits extended neighborhood relations and an adaptive margin to learn more discriminative and well-separated representations for both old and emerging classes. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-100, Tiny ImageNet, and ImageNet-100 demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, establishing a scalable and effective solution for C-GCD.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a Virtual Category-Guided approach for Continual Generalized Category Discovery (C-GCD), combining Virtual Category Learning (VCL) with Expanded Neighborhood Contrastive Learning (ENCL) to handle ambiguous unlabeled samples, reduce prediction bias, and improve discriminative representation learning for both known and novel categories in sequential open-world settings.
AI.motivation: C-GCD faces a bottleneck where ambiguous unlabeled samples cannot be confidently assigned to known classes or reliably grouped as novel ones, causing brittle pseudo-labeling and biased learning toward familiar categories.
AI.method: Adapts Virtual Category Learning (VCL) to continual setting—identifies uncertain samples and assigns them to temporary virtual categories to avoid noisy labels and improve data utilization. Augments with Expanded Neighborhood Contrastive Learning (ENCL) using extended neighborhood relations and an adaptive margin for more discriminative, well-separated representations across sessions.
AI.result: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods on CIFAR-100, Tiny ImageNet, and ImageNet-100 benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach provides a scalable and effective solution for C-GCD by safely learning from uncertain unlabeled data and enhancing class separation in continual discovery.

title: Geometry-aware Depth-guided Representation Learning for Structure-preserving Low-light Image Enhancement
summary: Low-light degradation reduces image visibility and weakens structural cues that are important for visual representation and scene understanding. Existing low-light image enhancement methods mainly focus on appearance restoration, while insufficiently exploiting scene geometry to preserve structural consistency. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a Depth-guided Multi-scale Attention Network (DMSA-Net) for geometry-aware low-light image enhancement. DMSA-Net introduces depth-related structural priors into low-light representation learning through reflectance-geometry interaction. A Retinex-based decomposition module is first used to obtain illumination-invariant reflectance representations, from which depth cues are inferred to characterize scene structure under degraded illumination. A multi-scale depth-guided fusion strategy is then embedded into a hierarchical encoder-decoder architecture, where depth-aware attention adaptively integrates geometric and appearance features. Experiments on several benchmark datasets show that DMSA-Net achieves effective low-light restoration while improving structural preservation. Moreover, we construct LOL-D, a depth-augmented low-light dataset, to facilitate research on geometry-aware low-light vision.

AI.tldr: DMSA-Net is a depth-guided multi-scale attention network that uses reflectance-geometry interaction and depth-aware attention to enhance low-light images while preserving structural consistency, validated on benchmark datasets and a newly constructed LOL-D dataset.
AI.motivation: Existing low-light enhancement methods focus on appearance restoration but insufficiently exploit scene geometry to preserve structural consistency, limiting performance in visual representation and scene understanding tasks.
AI.method: DMSA-Net uses Retinex-based decomposition to obtain illumination-invariant reflectance, infers depth cues from reflectance, and employs a multi-scale depth-guided fusion strategy with depth-aware attention in a hierarchical encoder-decoder to integrate geometric and appearance features.
AI.result: Effective low-light restoration with improved structural preservation; also introduces LOL-D, a depth-augmented low-light dataset.
AI.conclusion: DMSA-Net addresses geometry-aware low-light enhancement by incorporating depth-related structural priors, achieving both appearance restoration and structural consistency.

title: Comparison of Loss Functions for Robust Deep Learning-based Echocardiography Segmentation when Learning with Partially Labelled Data from Multiple Domains
comment: Accepted for publication at the Journal of Machine Learning for Biomedical Imaging (MELBA) https://melba-journal.org/2026:022
summary:
Echocardiography is the first imaging modality used for assessing cardiac function, and accurate segmentation of cardiac structures is essential for deriving biomarkers. However, the development of effective automated segmentation models for multiple cardiac structures is challenged by the difficulty of training on datasets from different sources that are often partially-labelled. This study aims to address this challenge by evaluating the performance of three loss functions - adaptive categorical cross entropy (aCCE) loss, marginal loss, and the adaptive binary cross entropy (aBCE) loss - in handling partially-labelled data. We conduct a comprehensive comparison of these loss functions across multiple scenarios and network architectures: intra-domain and inter-domain tasks, with both single and multiple partial-labels, and varying proportions of fully-labelled to partially-labelled data.
  Our experiments reveal that all three loss functions exhibit strong performance in intra-domain segmentation tasks, effectively handling label variations within the same domain. For inter-domain tasks, where models are trained on datasets with a domain shift, the aBCE and marginal losses show superior performance when dealing with the case of one label being missing from some training examples. In scenarios involving more than one label being missing, marginal loss outperforms the other methods, demonstrating its robustness in such complex conditions. These results highlight the strengths of each loss function depending on the labelling scenario, emphasizing the importance of selecting the appropriate loss function to optimize model performance. This study represents the first investigation of techniques for handling partially-labelled data from multiple different domains in echocardiography segmentation and provides a comprehensive comparison of loss-based solutions.

AI.tldr: This study compares three loss functions (aCCE, marginal, aBCE) for handling partially-labelled multi-domain echocardiography data, finding that aBCE and marginal losses perform best for inter-domain tasks, with marginal loss excelling when multiple labels are missing.
AI.motivation: Developing automated segmentation models for multiple cardiac structures is challenged by partially-labelled datasets from different sources, and no prior investigation has addressed how to handle such partially-labelled multi-domain data in echocardiography segmentation.
AI.method: The authors evaluate three loss functions—adaptive categorical cross entropy (aCCE), marginal loss, and adaptive binary cross entropy (aBCE)—across intra-domain and inter-domain tasks, with single/multiple partial labels and varying proportions of fully- to partially-labelled data, using multiple network architectures.
AI.result: All three loss functions perform well intra-domain; for inter-domain tasks, aBCE and marginal losses outperform aCCE when one label is missing; marginal loss excels when multiple labels are missing, demonstrating robustness in complex partial-label scenarios.
AI.conclusion: Selection of loss function is critical for optimizing model performance in partially-labelled multi-domain echocardiography segmentation, with marginal loss being most robust for complex missing-label conditions.

title: Unsupervised Pixel-Level Semantic Left-Right Understanding of In-the-Wild Images
summary: While various works address reflective symmetry understanding in 3D data and images, pixel-level semantic left-right prediction of in-the-wild images remains challenging, due to certain difficulties including the lack of 3D information, occlusion, object pose variation, partiality, etc. In this work, we propose an unsupervised learning framework to tackle this challenge. Leveraging recent advances in vertex-wise semantic left-right understanding of 3D data, our unsupervised learning method jointly utilises 3D shape and image datasets to infer pixel-wise semantic left-right predictions in single-view images. In particular, we show that a medium-scale 3D shape dataset comprising mainly of human- and quadruped animal-like shapes, combined with diverse in-the-wild image data, are sufficient to achieve high-quality semantic left-right prediction in images, even for entirely unseen 3D object categories, such as cars or trains. Overall, our approach achieves superior performance in dense pixel-wise semantic left-right predictions on both rendered and in-the-wild image datasets when compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

AI.tldr: An unsupervised learning framework that uses 3D shape data to predict pixel-level semantic left-right in single-view in-the-wild images, achieving state-of-the-art results.
AI.motivation: Pixel-level semantic left-right prediction in in-the-wild images remains challenging due to lack of 3D information, occlusion, pose variation, and partiality. Existing works address reflective symmetry in 3D data but not dense semantic left-right prediction in 2D images.
AI.method: An unsupervised learning framework that jointly utilizes 3D shape datasets (human- and quadruped-like shapes) and diverse in-the-wild image data to infer pixel-wise semantic left-right predictions, leveraging vertex-wise semantic left-right understanding from 3D data.
AI.result: Achieves superior performance in dense pixel-wise semantic left-right predictions on both rendered and in-the-wild image datasets compared to state-of-the-art methods. Generalizes to unseen 3D object categories (e.g., cars, trains).
AI.conclusion: A medium-scale 3D shape dataset combined with diverse in-the-wild images is sufficient for high-quality semantic left-right prediction, even for object categories not seen during training.

title: RUFNet: Query-Guided Support Mask Refinement and Uncertainty Fusion based on Hybrid Mamba for Few-Shot Brain Tumor Segmentation
summary: Few-shot brain tumor segmentation remains challenging due to noisy support masks, inter-patient variations between support and query images, and the lack of pixel-wise confidence estimation. This study proposes RUFNet, a Hybrid Mamba-based few-shot framework that combines support mask refinement with uncertainty-aware posterior fusion. To preserve support-query dependencies with manageable cost, RUFNet adopts a Hybrid Mamba interaction backbone with linear complexity. To reduce support-mask noise, an Attention-Guided Mask Refinement module (AGMR) uses query features to recalibrate support masks and improve prototype consistency. To handle ambiguous predictions, an Uncertainty-Aware Posterior Fusion module (UAPF) estimates pixel-wise variance and adaptively balances few-shot predictions with query-aligned priors. On the Brain Tumor Segmentation Challenge (BraTS) 2020 dataset, RUFNet achieves Dice coefficients of 84.3% and 86.1% in the 1-way 1-shot and 1-way 5-shot settings, respectively, outperforming the compared state-of-the-art methods. These results suggest that Hybrid Mamba interaction, mask refinement and uncertainty modelling can improve the robustness of few-shot medical image segmentation. The official implementation code is available at https://github.com/hdy6438/RUFNet.

AI.tldr: RUFNet is a Hybrid Mamba-based few-shot brain tumor segmentation framework that combines support mask refinement (AGMR) with uncertainty-aware posterior fusion (UAPF), achieving state-of-the-art Dice scores of 84.3% (1-shot) and 86.1% (5-shot) on BraTS 2020.
AI.motivation: Few-shot brain tumor segmentation suffers from noisy support masks, inter-patient variations between support and query images, and lack of pixel-wise confidence estimation.
AI.method: RUFNet employs (1) a Hybrid Mamba interaction backbone for support-query dependencies with linear complexity, (2) an Attention-Guided Mask Refinement (AGMR) module that uses query features to recalibrate support masks, and (3) an Uncertainty-Aware Posterior Fusion (UAPF) module that estimates pixel-wise variance and balances few-shot predictions with query-aligned priors.
AI.result: On BraTS 2020, RUFNet achieves Dice coefficients of 84.3% (1-way 1-shot) and 86.1% (1-way 5-shot), outperforming state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: Hybrid Mamba interaction, mask refinement, and uncertainty modelling improve the robustness of few-shot medical image segmentation.

title: Consistent and Editable: A Balanced Framework for Text-Guided Video Editing
summary: Recently, diffusion models have achieved considerable success in the text-guided video editing domain. However, existing works often struggle to balance the trade-off between temporal consistency and editability in video editing, with consistency and editability typically being inversely related. To address this, we propose a high-quality video editing framework enhanced for consistency and editability, named EquiEdit, which improves coordinatively the temporal consistency and editability of the edited videos while achieving a balance between the two. In terms of temporal consistency, the proposed temporal Mamba module with a tailored temporal-aware scanning scans fused video sequences following four designed directions, effectively enhancing the inter-frame consistency of edited videos. For editability, we design a noise injection strategy based on the spectral transformation to increase editing flexibility, where the Fourier transform is used to preserve the hidden structure in the initial latent noise used for editing, ensuring inter-frame consistency of the edited video and fidelity to the input video. Extensive qualitative and quantitative experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in terms of temporal consistency and editability, as well as its great fidelity to the input video itself.

AI.tldr: EquiEdit is a video editing framework that coordinatively improves temporal consistency and editability using a temporal Mamba module with directional scanning and a Fourier-based noise injection strategy.
AI.motivation: Existing text-guided video editing methods struggle to balance temporal consistency and editability, as these two properties are typically inversely related.
AI.method: (1) A temporal Mamba module with a tailored temporal-aware scanning that follows four designed directions to enhance inter-frame consistency. (2) A noise injection strategy based on spectral transformation using Fourier transform to preserve hidden structure in initial latent noise, increasing editing flexibility while ensuring consistency and fidelity.
AI.result: Extensive qualitative and quantitative experiments demonstrate effectiveness in temporal consistency, editability, and fidelity to the input video.
AI.conclusion: EquiEdit achieves a balanced trade-off between temporal consistency and editability in text-guided video editing, outperforming existing methods.

title: LangLoc: "Tell Me What You See"
comment: Accepted at the European Conference of Computer Vision (ECCV) 2026
summary: We tackle fine-grained indoor localization from natural language: given a free-form description of one's surroundings, estimate the observer's 2D position and heading within a known 3D environment. Language queries are lightweight, privacy-preserving, and need no camera - yet prior work stops at coarse scene retrieval and cannot resolve an intra-scene pose. We close this gap with LangLoc, a three-stage pipeline that (i) retrieves the correct scene via a dual-branch GATv2 encoder with CLIP semantic features, surpassing the previous best by 8 percentage points in Top-1 recall; (ii) estimates position and heading by scoring a dense floor grid through ray-cast object visibility, reaching a median error of 0.95 m; and (iii) resolves residual ambiguity through a Bayesian dialog module that asks targeted yes/no questions and updates a pose posterior until the location is pinpointed. To support this task we contribute a benchmark of $13{,}000{+}$ pose-indexed natural-language descriptions over $1{,}300{+}$ indoor 3D scans.

AI.tldr: LangLoc is a three-stage pipeline for fine-grained indoor localization from natural language descriptions, achieving scene retrieval (8 pp Top-1 improvement over prior work), pose estimation (0.95m median error), and residual ambiguity resolution via Bayesian dialog, supported by a new benchmark of 13,000+ descriptions over 1,300+ 3D scans.
AI.motivation: Prior work stops at coarse scene retrieval and cannot resolve intra-scene pose (fine-grained 2D position and heading) from free-form language queries, leaving a gap in privacy-preserving, camera-free indoor localization.
AI.method: Three-stage pipeline: (i) dual-branch GATv2 encoder with CLIP semantic features for scene retrieval; (ii) ray-cast object visibility scoring on a dense floor grid for pose estimation; (iii) Bayesian dialog module with targeted yes/no questions to resolve residual pose ambiguity.
AI.result: Scene retrieval surpasses prior best by 8 percentage points in Top-1 recall; pose estimation achieves a median error of 0.95 m.
AI.conclusion: LangLoc enables fine-grained indoor localization from natural language alone, closing the gap between coarse scene retrieval and precise intra-scene pose estimation, with potential for lightweight, privacy-preserving applications.

title: RADIANCE: Relative Adaptive Denoising with IP-Adapter for Novel Concept Enhancement
summary: Text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models have achieved striking progress but still struggle to synthesize rare concepts involving unusual attribute-object pairings, often resulting in concept omission or semantic drift where a dominant entity overwhelms the generation. Tracing these failures to a lack of compositional balance during the denoising trajectory, we propose RADIANCE, a training-free framework that treats inference as a closed-loop feedback process. RADIANCE augments pretrained backbones with three modular components: (1) a Compositional Similarity Monitor (CSM) that tracks the emergence of objects and attributes in intermediate latents via CLIP-based feedback; (2) a Bidirectional Scale Controller (BSC) that applies a reactive "restoring force" using positive and negative IP-Adapter scales to rebalance biased trajectories; and (3) a Feedback Guidance Scheduler (FGS) that coordinates these updates across timesteps without additional training. We further extend the framework to multi-object prompts via Delayed Adapter Activation (DAA) and Layer-wise Alternating Guidance (LAG) to prevent premature concept fusion. By overlapping monitoring and denoising through pipelined execution, RADIANCE maintains competitive latency while significantly enhancing the per-sample success rate and effective throughput. Experiments on RareBench and T2I-CompBench demonstrate that RADIANCE consistently enhances compositional alignment and perceptual quality over state-of-the-art baselines.

AI.tldr: RADIANCE is a training-free framework that enhances compositional balance in text-to-image diffusion models through CLIP-based monitoring, bidirectional scale control, and feedback-guided scheduling, improving synthesis of rare attribute-object pairings without additional training.
AI.motivation: T2I diffusion models struggle to synthesize rare concepts involving unusual attribute-object pairings, suffering from concept omission or semantic drift due to lack of compositional balance during denoising.
AI.method: RADIANCE augments pretrained backbones with three components: (1) Compositional Similarity Monitor (CSM) for CLIP-based feedback tracking, (2) Bidirectional Scale Controller (BSC) applying positive/negative IP-Adapter scales as restoring force, and (3) Feedback Guidance Scheduler (FGS) coordinating updates across timesteps. Extended with Delayed Adapter Activation (DAA) and Layer-wise Alternating Guidance (LAG) for multi-object prompts, plus pipelined execution for latency efficiency.
AI.result: Experiments on RareBench and T2I-CompBench show RADIANCE consistently improves compositional alignment and perceptual quality over state-of-the-art baselines while maintaining competitive latency and enhancing per-sample success rate and effective throughput.
AI.conclusion: Treating inference as a closed-loop feedback process effectively addresses compositional imbalance in T2I diffusion models, enabling reliable synthesis of rare attribute-object combinations without retraining.

title: TimeThink: Reasoning with Time for Video LLMs
summary: Video reasoning requires models to identify and verify temporally localized evidence within long video sequences. Recent Video Large Language Models (Video-LLMs) have shown promising reasoning abilities when aligned with reinforcement learning, yet existing approaches typically rely on outcome-based rewards that supervise only the final prediction. Such supervision provides limited guidance on how models should discover the relevant temporal evidence during intermediate reasoning. In this work, we propose TimeThink, a reinforcement learning framework that explicitly guides temporal evidence discovery in Video-LLMs. Our key idea is to treat temporal clue steps as the fundamental optimization primitive of video reasoning, where each reasoning step references a candidate time interval in the video. We introduce a step-wise temporal process reward that provides localized credit assignment for these clues and a joint process--outcome optimization objective that balances reasoning fidelity with task correctness. To enable scalable training, we construct TimeThink-RFT-20K, a dataset with automatically derived temporal evidence segments. Extensive experiments across video reasoning, temporal grounding, and general video understanding benchmarks show that TimeThink consistently improves both temporal localization and reasoning performance, achieving state-of-the-art results among open-source video RL models.

AI.tldr: TimeThink is a reinforcement learning framework that improves video reasoning in Video-LLMs by using step-wise temporal process rewards to guide evidence discovery, achieving SOTA results across multiple video benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing Video-LLMs aligned with reinforcement learning rely on outcome-based rewards that only supervise final predictions, providing insufficient guidance for models to discover temporally relevant evidence during intermediate reasoning steps.
AI.method: TimeThink treats temporal clue steps as the optimization primitive of video reasoning, where each reasoning step references a candidate time interval. It introduces a step-wise temporal process reward for localized credit assignment and a joint process-outcome optimization objective that balances reasoning fidelity with task correctness. The framework uses a constructed dataset TimeThink-RFT-20K with automatically derived temporal evidence segments.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art results among open-source video RL models across video reasoning, temporal grounding, and general video understanding benchmarks. Consistently improves both temporal localization and reasoning performance.
AI.conclusion: Providing process-level supervision for temporal evidence discovery significantly improves Video-LLMs' reasoning capabilities compared to outcome-only rewards.

title: Be Indiscrete: The Benefits of Learning Continuous Spine Degeneration Severity Scores
summary: Lumbar spine degeneration is a major contributor to chronic low back pain and is routinely assessed on MRI using ordinal grading systems, e.g. normal, mild, moderate, severe. Consequently, most approaches to train models to grade these MRIs formulate grading as a multi-class classification problem, treating ordinal grades as categorical, ignoring differences in misclassification severity, and imposing hard decision boundaries on a continuous disease process. This work explores modeling spinal degeneration as a continuous severity ranking problem. We introduce SpineRankNet, a framework that learns scalar severity scores from lumbar spinal MRI, and compare it against multi-class classification and ordinal regression. Using multiple degeneration measures from the Genodisc dataset, we show that a model trained using a ranking loss to produce a continuous score enables fine-grained ordering of MRI scans. Furthermore, the ordinal grading classes can be recovered from the score with comparable accuracy to those from a model trained directly for classification. The score learned by ranking even improves discrimination between more distant classes. Source code is available at https://github.com/spinetools/spineranknet.

AI.tldr: SpineRankNet learns continuous severity scores for lumbar spine degeneration from MRI, outperforming categorical classification and ordinal regression approaches by modeling degeneration as a ranking problem rather than discrete classes.
AI.motivation: Traditional ordinal grading systems (normal/mild/moderate/severe) for lumbar spine degeneration treat continuous disease processes as discrete categories, ignoring differences in misclassification severity and imposing hard decision boundaries.
AI.method: SpineRankNet uses a ranking loss to learn scalar severity scores from lumbar spinal MRI, compared against multi-class classification and ordinal regression baselines on the Genodisc dataset.
AI.result: The ranking-based continuous score enables fine-grained ordering of MRI scans, recovers ordinal grades with comparable accuracy to direct classification, and improves discrimination between more distant classes.
AI.conclusion: Modeling spinal degeneration as a continuous severity ranking problem is more appropriate than categorical classification, providing both fine-grained scoring and preserving ordinal grade utility.

title: Semantic Video Communication via Multi-Scale Convolution and Dynamic Routing for Next-Generation Networks
comment: Accepted at the AAAI 2026 Workshop on AI for Time Series (AI4TS)
summary: The exponential growth of video traffic demands novel semantic communication paradigms that transmit meaning rather than raw bits. We present a generative AI-enabled framework for semantic video communication addressing two critical challenges: efficient hierarchical temporal modeling for bandwidth-constrained transmission and robust semantic alignment between video content and natural language queries at network edge devices. Our approach introduces a multi-scale temporal convolutional encoder that captures motion patterns across different temporal granularities with O(T) complexity suitable for resource-constrained IoT deployments. We further propose a capsule-based dynamic routing mechanism that iteratively refines segment-query associations, enabling flexible modeling of non-monotonic semantic alignments essential for goal-oriented communication. These components are unified through a multi-task learning objective optimizing temporal boundary regression, cross-modal alignment, and capsule diversity. Experiments on ActivityNet Captions demonstrate significant improvements, achieving 42.9% Recall@0.5 and 41.1% mean IoU while maintaining computational efficiency critical for edge deployment.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a generative AI-driven framework for semantic video communication that uses a multi-scale temporal convolutional encoder (O(T) complexity) and capsule-based dynamic routing for efficient hierarchical temporal modeling and robust semantic alignment, achieving strong results on ActivityNet Captions (42.9% Recall@0.5, 41.1% mean IoU) while remaining suitable for edge deployment.
AI.motivation: The exponential growth of video traffic necessitates new semantic communication paradigms that transmit meaning instead of raw bits, and existing methods struggle with efficient temporal modeling under bandwidth constraints and robust semantic alignment between video and natural language queries on edge devices.
AI.method: A generative AI-enabled framework integrating (1) a multi-scale temporal convolutional encoder for hierarchical motion pattern capture with O(T) complexity, (2) a capsule-based dynamic routing mechanism for iterative refinement of segment-query associations enabling non-monotonic semantic alignment, and (3) a multi-task learning objective jointly optimizing temporal boundary regression, cross-modal alignment, and capsule diversity.
AI.result: On ActivityNet Captions, the method achieves 42.9% Recall@0.5 and 41.1% mean IoU while maintaining computational efficiency suitable for edge deployment.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework effectively addresses semantic video communication challenges for resource-constrained IoT environments by combining efficient temporal encoding with flexible semantic alignment mechanisms, advancing goal-oriented communication paradigms.

title: Green for Go, Red for No: Visual Grounding via Semantic Segmentation for VLA Navigation Policies
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robot navigation from natural language and visual goals, but remain susceptible to perceptual distractions and ambiguous scene interpretations. This paper presents the first empirical evaluation of visual grounding for VLA navigation policies. We propose a real-time segmentation-based grounding method that highlights traversable areas in green and non-traversable areas in red using SegFormer. Two variants are evaluated: observation-only segmentation and joint observation-goal augmentation. Using OmniVLA on the Grand Tour dataset, we show that visual grounding reduces the mean waypoint error by 27-44% at the farthest waypoint, depending on the instruction length. The benefits are greater for long instructions than for short instructions, and grounding provides little improvement for image goals. Normalized error analysis indicates that grounding primarily acts as a trajectory length regularizer, reducing the predicted path length by 30% without improving per-unit-distance reasoning. Our results indicate that visual grounding offers a simple, computationally inexpensive method to improve VLA navigation without model retraining, although it cannot compensate for missing training signals in out-of-distribution instructions.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates visual grounding for VLA navigation policies by overlaying segmentation-based traversability cues (green/red) on observations. Using OmniVLA on the Grand Tour dataset, grounding reduces waypoint error by 27-44% for farthest waypoints, primarily by acting as a trajectory length regularizer (reducing path length by 30%) rather than improving per-unit-distance reasoning. The method is simple, computationally cheap, and requires no retraining, but fails on out-of-distribution instructions.
AI.motivation: VLA models for robot navigation are susceptible to perceptual distractions and ambiguous scene interpretations, and no prior work has empirically evaluated visual grounding for VLA navigation policies.
AI.method: A real-time segmentation-based grounding method using SegFormer that highlights traversable areas in green and non-traversable areas in red. Two variants are tested: observation-only segmentation and joint observation-goal augmentation, evaluated with OmniVLA on the Grand Tour dataset.
AI.result: Visual grounding reduces mean waypoint error by 27-44% at the farthest waypoint, with greater benefits for long vs. short instructions and little improvement for image goals. Grounding reduces predicted path length by 30% but does not improve per-unit-distance reasoning.
AI.conclusion: Visual grounding is a simple, computationally inexpensive method to improve VLA navigation without model retraining, but cannot compensate for missing training signals in out-of-distribution instructions.

title: UNIVERSE: Unified Video Action Models for Autonomous Driving with Flexible Mask-Modulated Modality Generation
summary: World Action Models (WAMs) have shown strong potential for improving action generalization in autonomous driving by using future video prediction as dense supervision for scene dynamics and temporal causality. However, it remains unclear which architecture better transfers video-modeling benefits to trajectory generation. Existing cascaded or dual-DiT designs separate video imagination from action prediction, weakening the transfer of video-learned world dynamics to the trajectory branch: the action model may still overfit dataset-specific driving priors, while the video model only indirectly regularizes planning. We propose UNIVERSE, a unified video-action model built upon a single mask-modulated Diffusion Transformer. By co-training future video latents and ego-trajectory tokens within shared generative parameters, UNIVERSE allows dense video supervision to directly shape trajectory denoising, leading to stronger cross-domain action generalization. To ensure causal validity and efficient deployment, we introduce a Modality-Decoupling Visibility Mask, which shares historical context across modalities while blocking mutual attention between future video and trajectory tokens. This prevents future-target leakage and enables trajectory-only inference by removing future-video denoising at test time, achieving a $4.3\times$ speedup over joint video-action rollout while maintaining comparable planning accuracy. The same model also supports video-only and joint video-action rollouts. Experiments show that UNIVERSE achieves 91.0 PDMS on NAVSIM (vs. 89.6 for the Two-DiT variant), and demonstrates strong zero-shot transfer to nuScenes and Bench2Drive without fine-tuning, while ablations confirm the importance of single-DiT unification, video co-training, and mask-based modality decoupling.

AI.tldr: UNIVERSE is a unified video-action model using a single mask-modulated Diffusion Transformer that co-trains future video latents and ego-trajectory tokens, enabling dense video supervision to directly shape trajectory denoising for stronger cross-domain action generalization in autonomous driving. It introduces a Modality-Decoupling Visibility Mask to prevent future-target leakage and supports trajectory-only inference with 4.3× speedup, achieving 91.0 PDMS on NAVSIM and strong zero-shot transfer.
AI.motivation: Existing cascaded or dual-DiT designs separate video prediction from action prediction, weakening the transfer of video-learned world dynamics to the trajectory branch — the action model may overfit dataset-specific driving priors while video model only indirectly regularizes planning.
AI.method: UNIVERSE uses a single mask-modulated Diffusion Transformer to jointly co-train future video latents and ego-trajectory tokens within shared generative parameters. It introduces a Modality-Decoupling Visibility Mask that shares historical context across modalities while blocking mutual attention between future video and trajectory tokens to prevent future-target leakage and enable efficient deployment.
AI.result: Achieves 91.0 PDMS on NAVSIM (vs. 89.6 Two-DiT variant), strong zero-shot transfer to nuScenes and Bench2Drive without fine-tuning, 4.3× speedup for trajectory-only inference over joint video-action rollout.
AI.conclusion: Single-DiT unification, video co-training, and mask-based modality decoupling are critical for improving action generalization and efficiency in world action models for autonomous driving.

title: Fully Rotation-Equivariant Spectral-Spatial Learning for Multispectral Object Detection
summary: Existing multispectral detectors are limited by discrete spectral processing, a scale-dependent shift in the relative reliability of spectral and spatial cues across pyramid levels, and the lack of explicit rotation-equivariant geometric priors for arbitrarily oriented objects. To tackle these limitations, we propose FressDet, a fully rotation-equivariant spectral-spatial learning framework for multispectral object detection, capable of capturing the continuous, ordered nature of spectral structure and enabling reliable spectral-spatial fusion across pyramid levels under arbitrary in-plane rotations. FressDet integrates three complementary components. Spectral Implicit Warp (SpeIW) enables query-based spectral resampling via a coordinate-conditioned implicit field, yielding a monotone, order-preserving warp. Rotation-Equivariant Consistency Weighting (ReCoW) adaptively fuses spectral and spatial branches based on branch reliability, reinforcing informative cues while suppressing noise across pyramid levels. The oriented-aware head exploits group-indexed features to stably predict oriented objects without parameter replication. Taken together, FressDet learns more discriminative and robust spectral-spatial representations even under rotational perturbations. By achieving state-of-the-art performance with 93% fewer parameters on three public benchmarks, FressDet demonstrates its effectiveness and generalizability.

AI.tldr: FressDet is a fully rotation-equivariant spectral-spatial learning framework for multispectral object detection that integrates Spectral Implicit Warp, Rotation-Equivariant Consistency Weighting, and an orientation-aware head to achieve state-of-the-art performance with 93% fewer parameters across three benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing multispectral detectors suffer from discrete spectral processing, scale-dependent shifts in spectral-spatial cue reliability across pyramid levels, and a lack of explicit rotation-equivariant geometric priors for arbitrarily oriented objects.
AI.method: FressDet proposes three components: (1) Spectral Implicit Warp (SpeIW) for query-based spectral resampling via a coordinate-conditioned implicit field; (2) Rotation-Equivariant Consistency Weighting (ReCoW) for adaptive fusion of spectral and spatial branches based on reliability across pyramid levels; (3) an orientation-aware head using group-indexed features for stable oriented object prediction without parameter replication.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on three public benchmarks while using 93% fewer parameters than existing methods, and demonstrates robust spectral-spatial representations under rotational perturbations.
AI.conclusion: FressDet effectively addresses key limitations of multispectral detectors through rotation-equivariant design and reliable spectral-spatial fusion, proving both effective and generalizable.

title: Shifting from Discrete to Continuous Reference Data: QSM-Derived Horizontal Tree Biomass Distribution for Deep Learning Biomass Estimation
summary: Conventional modeling approaches for LiDAR-based above-ground biomass (AGB) estimation rely on discrete plot-level inventory aggregates. This methodology introduces boundary-effect uncertainties that may severely degrade model performance within small field plots. To solve this limitation, we evaluate a Horizontal Biomass Distribution (HBD) reference mapped continuously from Quantitative Structure Models (QSMs). We trained a sparse 3D U-Net on simulated broadleaved forest structures using three AGB reference types: a standard forest inventory (FI) plot-level aggregate, an edge-effect-free QSM plot-level aggregate, and a continuous HBD mapping. Evaluating training plot sizes scaling from 100 to 2500 $m^2$ , QSM-based models systematically outperformed FI approaches at small plot sizes. Specifically, for 100 $m^2$ plots, the HBD reference reduced the relative root mean square error (RRMSE) by 16.84 $\pm$ 4.37 % and increased $R^2$ by 0.22 $\pm$ 0.05 against the FI baseline. By replacing plot level aggregates with HBDs as AGB reference, this methodology corrects for edge-effects and shows that using an HBD-based reference enhances model performance for small plot sizes.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using continuous Horizontal Biomass Distribution (HBD) references derived from Quantitative Structure Models (QSMs) instead of discrete plot-level aggregates for LiDAR-based AGB estimation. The HBD approach reduces edge-effect uncertainties and significantly improves model performance for small plot sizes (e.g., 16.84% RRMSE reduction for 100 m² plots).
AI.motivation: Conventional plot-level aggregate modeling for LiDAR-based AGB estimation suffers from boundary-effect uncertainties that degrade model performance, especially in small field plots.
AI.method: Trained a sparse 3D U-Net on simulated broadleaved forest structures using three AGB reference types: standard forest inventory (FI) plot-level aggregate, edge-effect-free QSM plot-level aggregate, and continuous HBD mapping. Evaluated training plot sizes from 100 to 2500 m².
AI.result: QSM-based models outperformed FI approaches at small plot sizes. For 100 m² plots, HBD reference reduced RRMSE by 16.84 ± 4.37% and increased R² by 0.22 ± 0.05 compared to FI baseline.
AI.conclusion: Replacing plot-level aggregates with continuous HBD references corrects edge-effects and enhances model performance for small plot sizes in LiDAR-based AGB estimation.

title: Probing Geospatial SSL Representations with Environmental Signals
summary: Self-supervised learning (SSL) is designed to learn generic, transferable representations rather than representations optimized for a single task. Most geospatial benchmarks evaluate representations solely through downstream tasks, providing limited insight into the information encoded within the representation itself. We ask a different question: do SSL representations of satellite imagery preserve statistical associations with environmental variables that co-vary with the imaging process? To answer this question, we probe SSL representations using co-located ERA5 reanalysis variables, a global dataset of physically consistent environmental variables, including temperature, precipitation, surface solar radiation, surface pressure, and volumetric soil water. These variables are physically related to the spectral reflectance and radar backscatter recorded by Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2, making them meaningful evaluation targets despite not being used during SSL pretraining. We complement this probing analysis with intrinsic representation metrics to characterize representation geometry and investigate how these properties relate to downstream performance and the encoding of environmental signals. Using DINO, MAE, and MoCo models trained under identical conditions, we show that representation-level metrics distinguish models with similar downstream benchmark performance, providing complementary information beyond task-driven benchmarks. We further find that the linear accessibility of environmental signals is associated with performance on environmentally dependent tasks in the PANGAEA benchmark. Finally, we release ERA5 annotations co-located with the SSL4EO dataset to enable physically grounded representation evaluation for future geospatial foundation models.

AI.tldr: The paper probes SSL representations of satellite imagery using ERA5 environmental variables to evaluate what information is encoded beyond downstream task performance, finding that representation-level metrics and environmental signal accessibility provide complementary insights for model evaluation.
AI.motivation: Most geospatial benchmarks evaluate SSL representations solely through downstream tasks, which provides limited insight into the information encoded within the representation itself. The authors ask whether SSL representations of satellite imagery preserve statistical associations with environmental variables that co-vary with the imaging process.
AI.method: The authors probe SSL representations (DINO, MAE, MoCo) using co-located ERA5 reanalysis variables (temperature, precipitation, surface solar radiation, surface pressure, volumetric soil water) and use intrinsic representation metrics to characterize representation geometry. They compare these with downstream benchmark performance on PANGAEA.
AI.result: Representation-level metrics distinguish models with similar downstream benchmark performance, providing complementary information. Linear accessibility of environmental signals is associated with performance on environmentally dependent tasks in the PANGAEA benchmark.
AI.conclusion: Probing with physically grounded environmental variables offers a complementary evaluation approach for geospatial SSL models. The authors release ERA5 annotations co-located with the SSL4EO dataset for future research.

title: Claim-Level Rubric Rewards for Video Caption Reinforcement Learning
summary: In this paper, we introduce Claim-Level Rubric Rewards (CuRe), a structured reward framework designed to address the reward-design bottleneck in reinforcement learning for dense video captioning. Existing reward designs generally fall into two categories: holistic response-level judgment across heterogeneous criteria, or alignment-based evaluation against reference captions. However, both paradigms suffer from fundamental limitations. Holistic rewards struggle to ensure factual accuracy and are prone to stylistic reward hacking, while reference-based rewards overly rely on rigid textual alignment, failing to preserve the completeness and diversity inherent to open-ended generation tasks. To address these challenges, CuRe reformulates reward modeling as fine-grained claim-level verification. Specifically, CuRe decomposes captions into category-aware atomic claims through a structured rubric, converting holistic evaluation into simpler and more reliable claim-level verification.

AI.tldr: CuRe introduces a structured reward framework using claim-level verification for dense video captioning, addressing limitations of holistic and reference-based reward designs.
AI.motivation: Existing reward designs (holistic response-level judgment and alignment-based evaluation) suffer from factual inaccuracy, stylistic reward hacking, and rigid textual alignment that undermines completeness and diversity in open-ended generation tasks.
AI.method: CuRe reformulates reward modeling as fine-grained claim-level verification by decomposing captions into category-aware atomic claims through a structured rubric, converting holistic evaluation into simpler claim-level verification.
AI.result: Not specified in the abstract.
AI.conclusion: CuRe provides a more reliable and fine-grained reward framework for reinforcement learning in dense video captioning, addressing key limitations of prior reward paradigms.

title: Is the Geometry Doing the Work? An Operating-Point Audit of Hierarchy in Hyperbolic Vision-Language Models
comment: 52 pages, 5 figures, Under review at TMLR
summary: Whether a hyperbolic representation model uses its geometry cannot be read off its curvature parameter: what matters is the dimensionless operating point $\sqrt{c}ρ$ and whether the radial and cone machinery is active there. We develop a battery of necessary-condition diagnostics and audit three published hyperbolic vision-language families -- MERU, HyCoCLIP, and PHyCLIP -- across released checkpoints and controlled interventions on a fixed GRIT snapshot, identifying three failure modes. First, curvature is not an active resource: the operating point stays near-Euclidean ($H(u)\approx 1$; no audited converged checkpoint reaches $\sqrt{c}ρ>1$), and releasing the curvature floor moves curvature and norms but keeps the operating point near-Euclidean, without substantial downstream degradation. Second, the cone and traversal machinery is measured inoperative: entailment cones are inactive, saturated, or misaligned, and graded traversal fails under controlled readouts, while directed radial depth is a bounded non-detection above shuffle-null controls at quantified sensitivity; the one surviving native-relation residual remains non-operative. Third, hierarchy-looking evaluations are underdetermined: taxonomy correlations are carried by angular distance, and coarse-retrieval gains track box/compositional supervision, not curvature. A mechanistic account explains why: the entailment objective admits a low-curvature, wide-cone shortcut, and a parameter-free aperture identity (cones saturate iff $\sqrt{c}ρ\le 2K$) locates the edge where every entailment-trained unclamped run settles; entailment-off runs show no arrest there. The shortcut is the dominant accelerator of collapse, not its sole cause. These formulations, as released, do not instantiate the radial/cone mechanism their geometry motivates; we distill the audit into a five-number geometry report for future hierarchy claims.

AI.tldr: Published hyperbolic vision-language models (MERU, HyCoCLIP, PHyCLIP) do not actually use their hyperbolic geometry: their operating points stay near-Euclidean, cone/traversal mechanisms are inoperative, and hierarchy-looking gains come from non-geometric sources like angular distance or box/compositional supervision. The paper diagnoses three failure modes, identifies a low-curvature shortcut explaining why training converges at a parameter-free saturation boundary, and proposes a five-number geometry report for auditing future hierarchy claims.
AI.motivation: To audit whether hyperbolic representation models genuinely exploit their geometric machinery (radial distance, entailment cones, traversal) rather than merely having a non-Euclidean curvature parameter, because curvature alone does not determine geometric behavior—the dimensionless operating point $\sqrt{c}ρ$ does.
AI.method: Develops a battery of necessary-condition diagnostics, applies them to three published hyperbolic VLM families (MERU, HyCoCLIP, PHyCLIP) across released checkpoints and controlled interventions on a fixed GRIT snapshot, plus a mechanistic analysis revealing a parameter-free aperture identity where cones saturate iff $\sqrt{c}ρ \le 2K$.
AI.result: (1) Curvature is not an active resource—operating point stays near-Euclidean ($H(u)\approx 1$, no $\sqrt{c}ρ>1$). (2) Cone and traversal machinery is inoperative—entailment cones are inactive/saturated/misaligned, graded traversal fails, directed radial depth is non-detection above shuffle-null. (3) Hierarchy evaluations are underdetermined—taxonomy correlations are carried by angular distance, retrieval gains track box/compositional supervision not curvature. The entailment objective admits a low-curvature, wide-cone shortcut converging at the saturation boundary.
AI.conclusion: These hyperbolic VLM formulations as released do not instantiate the radial/cone mechanism their geometry motivates; the audit is distilled into a five-number geometry report for evaluating future hierarchy claims.

title: FSDC-DETR: A Frequency-Spatial Domain Collaborative DETR for Small Object Detection
summary: Small object detection (SOD) remains a challenging task in real-world applications. Despite recent advances, existing detectors remain limited by rigid processing that entangle spatial aggregation with implicit frequency aliasing and truncation, leading to inadequate preservation of high-frequency components for SOD. To tackle these limitations, we propose a Frequency-Spatial Domain Collaborative Detection Transformer (FSDC-DETR), a novel collaborative framework that explicitly models complementary spatial and frequency representations. Specifically, we first introduce Dual-Branch Frequency-Spatial Adaptive Fusion (DBFSAF) to enhance frequency diversity and adaptively capture frequency-spatial domain discriminative representations. Building on these representations, a frequency-spatial interaction scheme is further explored within the hybrid encoder to enable progressive feature propagation to the decoder. In particular, structure-aware frequency-spatial aggregation is achieved through Shunt Frequency-Spatial Feature Fusion (SFS-FF), establishing bidirectional interaction and progressive cross-scale propagation between frequency and spatial representations for coherent discriminative modeling. Meanwhile, informative high-frequency responses are preserved during scale transitions through Frequency-Spatial Dynamic Downsampling (FSD-Down), thereby minimizing frequency degradation throughout multi-scale fusion for the precise SOD. Experimental results demonstrate that FSDC-DETR achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving AP by 6.4 on VisDrone-DET2019 and 6.6 on AITODv2, with gains of 6.8 and 6.9 AP for small objects. The code is available at github.com/nevereverinsomnia/FSDC-DETR.

AI.tldr: FSDC-DETR is a Frequency-Spatial Domain Collaborative Detection Transformer that improves small object detection by explicitly modeling complementary frequency and spatial representations through dual-branch adaptive fusion, interaction, dynamic downsampling, and cross-scale propagation, achieving state-of-the-art results on VisDrone-DET2019 and AITODv2.
AI.motivation: Existing detectors struggle with small object detection due to rigid processing that entangles spatial aggregation with implicit frequency aliasing and truncation, resulting in inadequate preservation of high-frequency components critical for SOD.
AI.method: Proposes FSDC-DETR with three key components: (1) Dual-Branch Frequency-Spatial Adaptive Fusion (DBFSAF) for frequency diversity and discriminative representation learning; (2) Shunt Frequency-Spatial Feature Fusion (SFS-FF) for bidirectional interaction and progressive cross-scale propagation in a hybrid encoder; (3) Frequency-Spatial Dynamic Downsampling (FSD-Down) to preserve high-frequency responses during scale transitions.
AI.result: State-of-the-art performance: +6.4 AP on VisDrone-DET2019 and +6.6 AP on AITODv2, with +6.8 and +6.9 AP gains specifically for small objects.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly modeling complementary frequency-spatial representations with dedicated frequency preservation mechanisms effectively addresses SOD limitations imposed by implicit aliasing and truncation in conventional detectors.

title: Topological Shape Representation for Aneurysm -- Bifurcation Detection
summary: Automated detection of intracranial aneurysms (IAs) from CT angiography (CTA) is severely hindered by high false-positive rates. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) rely on local pixel intensities, causing systematic confusion between saccular aneurysms and vascular bifurcations -- a problem especially acute for small lesions (<3 mm), where detection sensitivity falls below 60%. We propose a plug-and-play, topology-aware false-positive reduction framework evaluating the Smooth Euler Characteristic Transform (SECT) -- a directional representation encoding global 3D vascular geometry independently of intensity -- against persistence-based summaries (Persistence Images and Landscapes), tested on a stratified subset of the RSNA 2025 dataset. SECT achieves an AUC of 0.943, substantially outperforming direction-agnostic methods (AUC ~0.68), and exhibits a clinical performance inversion: it excels on the sub-3 mm cohort, maintaining 0.943 AUC and 78.5% sensitivity at 95% specificity. The representation is also scanner-agnostic, achieving 0.927 mean AUC under leave-one-scanner-out (LOGO) validation across four manufacturers. By capturing asymmetric geometric invariants rather than intensity profiles, SECT reliably resolves the primary structural confounder in IA detection, positioning it as a robust downstream filter for hybrid deep-learning diagnostic pipelines.

AI.tldr: A topology-aware false-positive reduction framework using the Smooth Euler Characteristic Transform (SECT) significantly improves intracranial aneurysm detection from CTA, especially for small lesions <3 mm, achieving AUC of 0.943 and outperforming direction-agnostic methods (AUC ~0.68).
AI.motivation: Automated IA detection from CTA suffers from high false-positive rates; CNNs systematically confuse saccular aneurysms with vascular bifurcations due to reliance on local pixel intensities, and detection sensitivity falls below 60% for small lesions (<3 mm).
AI.method: Proposes a plug-and-play, topology-aware false-positive reduction framework using SECT — a directional representation encoding global 3D vascular geometry independently of intensity — tested against persistence-based summaries (Persistence Images and Landscapes) on a stratified subset of the RSNA 2025 dataset, with leave-one-scanner-out (LOGO) validation across four manufacturers.
AI.result: SECT achieves AUC of 0.943, substantially outperforming direction-agnostic methods (AUC ~0.68); maintains 0.943 AUC and 78.5% sensitivity at 95% specificity for the sub-3 mm cohort; achieves 0.927 mean AUC under LOGO validation, demonstrating scanner-agnostic performance.
AI.conclusion: By capturing asymmetric geometric invariants rather than intensity profiles, SECT reliably resolves the primary structural confounder in IA detection, positioning it as a robust downstream filter for hybrid deep-learning diagnostic pipelines.

title: Causal-RetiGraph: Cross-Cohort Retinal Support and Same-Subject Pathway Analysis for Diabetic Retinopathy
summary: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a local retinal lesion process and a visible manifestation of systemic microvascular injury. Modern retinal AI can grade images accurately, but often leaves unanswered how local lesion evidence, retinal vascular structure, and systemic disease pathways are connected. This paper introduces \emph{Causal-RetiGraph}, a compact biomedical informatics framework that links retinal graph phenotypes with NHANES-anchored pathway modelling. The retinal-image fold constructs an interpretable $X1234$ phenotype from vessel maps, lesion evidence, image embeddings, and AutoMorph biomarkers through spatial $X_{12}$ and Jacobian $X_{34}$ branches. The NHANES fold models systemic exposures, covariates, a same-subject retinal mediator family $R^*$, and downstream outcome families. $X1234$ is used for retinal support and pathway prioritisation, while $R^*$ is used for participant-level pathway summaries. On the retinal fold, $X1234$ achieves 0.9055 binary DR accuracy and 0.9711 AUROC, with graded DR QWK of 0.8312. The results show that lesion and biomarker streams improve contextual retinal representation under scarce and imbalanced data. In NHANES, HbA1c, urine albumin, pulse pressure, fasting glucose, and systolic blood pressure are the strongest binary DR anchors. Participant-level pathway analysis identifies glycaemic--renal and glycaemic--haemodynamic pathways as the clearest mediator-style signals. These results suggest that retinal graph phenotypes can help prioritise systemic pathways in DR while preserving the distinction between image-derived support and same-subject mediation.

AI.tldr: Causal-RetiGraph is a biomedical informatics framework that links retinal graph phenotypes (X1234) with NHANES pathway modeling to connect local retinal lesion evidence with systemic disease pathways in diabetic retinopathy, achieving 0.9055 DR accuracy and identifying glycaemic–renal and glycaemic–haemodynamic as key mediator pathways.
AI.motivation: Modern retinal AI can grade DR images accurately but fails to explain how local lesion evidence, retinal vascular structure, and systemic disease pathways are interconnected.
AI.method: A two-fold framework: (1) retinal-image fold constructs an interpretable X1234 phenotype from vessel maps, lesions, embeddings, and AutoMorph biomarkers via spatial (X12) and Jacobian (X34) branches; (2) NHANES fold models systemic exposures, covariates, retinal mediator family R*, and outcome families, using X1234 for support/pathway prioritization and R* for participant-level summaries.
AI.result: X1234 achieves 0.9055 binary DR accuracy, 0.9711 AUROC, and graded DR QWK of 0.8312. HbA1c, urine albumin, pulse pressure, fasting glucose, and systolic BP are strongest binary DR anchors. Glycaemic–renal and glycaemic–haemodynamic pathways show clearest mediator signals.
AI.conclusion: Retinal graph phenotypes can help prioritize systemic pathways in DR while preserving the distinction between image-derived support and same-subject mediation.

title: Multiplayer Interactive World Models with Representation Autoencoders
summary: We introduce the first multiplayer world model for highly dynamic environments governed by complex physical interactions. Whereas single-player world models treat the other agents as part of the environment, ours conditions on the action streams of multiple agents, learning to attribute changes in the scene to the correct player and to stay coherent under arbitrary combinations of their actions. We study this problem in the game of Rocket League, where players compete and cooperate under fast, tightly coupled dynamics. Trained on 10,000 hours of gameplay collected with publicly available bots, our 5-billion-parameter latent diffusion model generates four-player matches in real time, producing 20 frames per second on a single Nvidia B200 GPU. Although trained only on short clips, its rollouts stay stable far beyond the training horizon: distributional quality holds steady out to five minutes, the longest horizon we measure, and in practice we observe rollouts continuing for hours with no sign of collapse. We systematically investigate the central design choices: the video codec, the generative objective, and the multiplayer conditioning scheme. In addition, we characterize how behavior changes with model and data scale, including the capabilities that emerge and the failure modes that persist. We further develop targeted evaluations that probe the model's physical understanding rather than visual appearance alone. To support continued research on multiplayer world models, we release our dataset, our full training and inference codebase, and a live demo.

AI.tldr: First multiplayer world model using a 5-billion-parameter latent diffusion model for Rocket League, trained on 10,000 hours of gameplay, generating stable four-player matches at 20 FPS on a single B200 GPU.
AI.motivation: Existing single-player world models treat other agents as part of the environment, failing to handle highly dynamic multi-agent scenarios with complex physical interactions. A multiplayer world model that conditions on multiple agents' action streams is needed.
AI.method: A 5-billion-parameter latent diffusion model trained on 10,000 hours of Rocket League gameplay with publicly available bots. Conditions on multi-agent action streams, uses a video codec, generative objective, and multiplayer conditioning scheme. Generates four-player matches at 20 FPS on a single Nvidia B200 GPU.
AI.result: Model generates real-time four-player matches (20 FPS). Rollouts remain stable far beyond training horizon: distributional quality holds for 5 minutes (longest measured), and continues for hours without collapse. Behavior systematically characterized across model/data scales.
AI.conclusion: Multiplayer world models are feasible for complex, physically dynamic environments. The work releases dataset, codebase, and demo to support continued research. Targeted evaluations probe physical understanding beyond visual appearance.
